````
## 2. Build tooling

### The jupyter-builder split (this is the big one)

`extension_migration.md:30-66`, section "Migrating to `jupyter-builder`":
&gt; JupyterLab's build tooling has moved out of the JupyterLab repository into a standalone package: `jupyter-builder` (PyPI) and `@jupyter/builder` (npm). Existing extensions continue to work, but we recommend migrating so your build no longer depends on a full JupyterLab installation.

**pyproject.toml** (`extension_migration.md:41-48`):
```toml
# Before
requires = ["hatchling&gt;=1.5.0", "jupyterlab&gt;=4.0.0,&lt;5", "hatch-nodejs-version&gt;=0.3.2"]
# After
requires = ["hatchling&gt;=1.5.0", "hatch-nodejs-version&gt;=0.3.2", "jupyter-builder&gt;=1.0.0"]
```

**package.json** (`extension_migration.md:50-66`):
```json
"@jupyter/builder": "^1.0.0"
```
```json
"build:labextension": "jupyter-builder build .",
"build:labextension:dev": "jupyter-builder build --development True .",
"watch:labextension": "jupyter-builder watch ."
```

`@jupyterlab/builder` **no longer exists**: CHANGELOG entry "Remove `@jupyterlab/builder` package and all references to it" (#18841), plus "Use `@jupyter/builder` instead of `@jupyterlab/builder`" (#18723) — both in the 4.6 cycle. Every in-repo extension `package.json` now pins `"@jupyter/builder": "^1.0.0-beta.1"` (e.g. `/Users/tel/git/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/galata/extension/package.json:52`).

Also in that migration section (`extension_migration.md:36`):
&gt; JupyterLab 4.6 also no longer depends on `setuptools` at runtime. If your extension uses `setuptools`-based packaging or build hooks, add `setuptools` to your own package requirements explicitly...

### `jupyter labextension develop --overwrite .` is **deprecated**

The docs now say `jupyter-builder develop`:

`extension_tutorial.md:211-218`:
```bash
pip install -ve .
# better:
jupyter-builder develop --overwrite .
```

`extension_dev.md:608-614`:
&gt; Build a prebuilt extension using the `jupyter-builder build` command. ... you can use the `jupyter-builder develop` command to create a link to your prebuilt output directory, similar to `pip install -e`:
```
jupyter-builder develop . --overwrite
```

Confirmed in code — `/Users/tel/git/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/labextensions.py:471-483`, `DevelopLabExtensionAlias`:
```
"""Compatibility alias: delegates to 'jupyter-builder develop'."""
description = "(deprecated) Develop labextension - use 'jupyter-builder develop' instead"
...
sys.exit(subprocess.call(["jupyter-builder", "develop"] + self._builder_args))
```
Same for `build` (`:455`) and `watch` (`:486`); registered as `"develop": (DevelopLabExtensionAlias, "(deprecated) Develop labextension")` at `:529`. So `jupyter labextension develop --overwrite .` still *works* but prints a yellow deprecation warning.

### `jlpm`

`extension_tutorial.md:322-357`: `jlpm add @jupyterlab/apputils @jupyterlab/application`, then `jlpm build`, or `jlpm watch`. `extension_tutorial.md:332-335`:
&gt; This tutorial uses `jlpm` to install JavaScript packages and run build commands, which is JupyterLab's bundled version of `yarn`. If you prefer, you can use another JavaScript package manager like `npm` or `yarn` itself.

`jlpm build` = `tsc` into `lib/` then `jupyter-builder build` into `&lt;pypkg&gt;/labextension/static` (`extension_tutorial.md:350-353`). jlpm is Yarn 3 since 4.0, requiring `.yarnrc.yml` with `nodeLinker: node-modules` and `.yarn/` in `.gitignore` (`extension_migration.md:501-530`). Repo root pins `"packageManager": "yarn@3.5.0"` (`package.json:144`).

### `jupyter server extension enable`

**Not mentioned anywhere in the docs.** A repo-wide grep of `docs/` for `server extension enable` / `jpserver_extensions` returns nothing. The docs only describe the declarative mechanism, in `/Users/tel/git/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/docs/source/developer/repo.md:91-94`:
&gt; ### Jupyter Server Configuration: `jupyter-config/`
&gt; This directory contains metadata distributed with the Python package that allows it to automatically enable the Jupyter server extension upon installation.

### Rspack replaces webpack

`extension_migration.md:68-76`:
&gt; In the upcoming 4.6, JupyterLab will use [Rspack](https://rspack.rs/) instead of [Webpack](https://webpack.js.org/) to build extensions. Since Rspack strives for compatibility with Webpack, no changes should be needed in most extensions... However, if an extension uses the experimental `webpackConfig` option, it may need to migrate its custom Webpack config to Rspack.

`extension_dev.md:591`: the `package.json` key is still spelled `webpackConfig` "for historical reasons... instead of `rspackConfig`."

## 3. Files / directories a frontend extension contains

Important caveat up front: **the JupyterLab docs in this checkout do not document the Python server-extension half at all.** `extension_dev.md` mentions server extensions only under `jupyterlab.discovery` (as a *companion package* pointer, `:471-511`). There is no `_jupyter_server_extension_points`, no `jupyter-config/jupyter_server_config.d/` guidance, no handler-writing guide anywhere under `docs/source/extension/`. All of that is punted to the template and to jupyter_server's own docs.

### What the tutorial shows (the `frontend` kind file listing)

`extension_tutorial.md:169-176`:
```
.copier-answers.yml  .github          .gitignore      .prettierignore     .yarnrc.yml
babel.config.js      jest.config.js   pyproject.toml  src                 ui-tests
binder               jupyterlab_apod  README.md       style               yarn.lock
CHANGELOG.md         LICENSE          RELEASE.md      tsconfig.json
install.json         package.json     setup.py        tsconfig.test.json
```
Note `install.json` and `setup.py` are present, `schema/` and `jupyter-config/` are **not** (the tutorial answered `N` to user settings and chose `frontend`).

### `package.json` → `jupyterlab` field (source extension), `extension_dev.md:296-306`

Schema lives at `github.com/jupyterlab/jupyter-builder/blob/main/src/metadata_schema.json`, "distributed in the `@jupyter/builder` package."

| key | doc ref |
|---|---|
| `extension` | `:311-319` — `true` if default export of `main` is the plugin/plugin list, or a path string like `"lib/foo"`. "A JupyterLab extension must have at least one of `jupyterlab.extension` or `jupyterlab.mimeExtension` set." (`:307`) |
| `mimeExtension` | `:323` |
| `themePath` | `:329-339` — e.g. `"style/theme.css"`; "An extension cannot bundle multiple theme plugins." |
| `schemaDir` | `:345-368` — `"schemaDir": "schema"`; plugin `&lt;pkg&gt;:&lt;name&gt;` reads `&lt;schemaDir&gt;/&lt;name&gt;.json`. "Please ensure that the schema files are included in the `files` metadata in `package.json`." |
| `disabledExtensions` | `:374-386` |
| `sharedPackages` | `:390-450` |
| `discovery` | `:471-545` |
| `outputDir` | **prebuilt-only**, `:560-573` |
| `webpackConfig` | **prebuilt-only**, `:575-604` |

Plus top-level (not under `jupyterlab`), `extension_dev.md:548-552`:
&gt; If your extension has a top-level `style` key in `package.json`, the CSS file it points to will be included on the page automatically. ... if your extension has a top-level `styleModule` key ... it will be imported (as a JavaScript module) instead.

**`outputDir`** (`:567-573`):
&gt; The `jupyterlab.outputDir` field gives the relative path to the directory where these JavaScript and other files should be placed. A copy of the `package.json` file with additional build metadata will be put in the `outputDir` and the JavaScript and other files that will be served are put into the `static` subdirectory.
```json
"jupyterlab": { "outputDir": "mypackage/labextension" }
```

**`sharedPackages`** (`:398-450`) — three booleans `bundled` (default `true`), `singleton` (default `false`), `strictVersion`; or `false` to not share at all. Recommended recipes: a **provider** of a token from a non-core package sets `"token-package": { "singleton": true }` (`:412-418`); consumers get the parallel recipe at `:428` / `:445`.

**`discovery`** (`:477-514`) — this is the one place server extensions surface. Full shape includes a `server` block:
```
"discovery": {
  "server": {
    "base": { "name": "&lt;the name of the server extension package&gt;" },
    "overrides": { "pip": { "name": "&lt;name on pip, if it differs&gt;" } },
    "managers": ["pip", "conda"]
  }
}
```
"Currently supported package managers are `pip` and `conda`." (`:541`)

### Distribution layout, `extension_dev.md:646-670`

- Prebuilt output goes to `&lt;sys-prefix&gt;/share/jupyter/labextensions/&lt;package-name&gt;` — `&lt;package-name&gt;` is the **JS** package name, so `@my-org/my-package` → `share/jupyter/labextensions/@my-org/my-package` (`:646`).
- `install.json` at that directory's top level (`:654-669`):
```json
{
  "packageManager": "python",
  "packageName": "mypackage",
  "uninstallInstructions": "Use your Python package manager (pip, conda, etc.) to uninstall the package mypackage"
}
```
- PyPI trove classifiers (`:678-690`), notably `Framework :: Jupyter :: JupyterLab :: Extensions :: Prebuilt`, which "is used by the extension manager to get the available extensions from PyPI.org" (`:696`).

### The server half — reconstructed from JupyterLab's own source (since the docs omit it)

- `/Users/tel/git/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/__init__.py:15-23` — the two hook functions:
```python
def _jupyter_server_extension_paths() -&gt; list[dict[str, str]]:
    return [{"module": "jupyterlab"}]

def _jupyter_server_extension_points() -&gt; list[dict[str, str | type]]:
    from .labapp import LabApp
    return [{"module": "jupyterlab", "app": LabApp}]
```
  (JupyterLab itself does **not** define `_jupyter_labextension_paths` — it ships its assets via `share/jupyter/lab/static` rather than as a labextension. The template's generated `__init__.py` is where `_jupyter_labextension_paths` lives.)
- `/Users/tel/git/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/jupyter-config/jupyter_server_config.d/jupyterlab.json`:
```json
{ "ServerApp": { "jpserver_extensions": { "jupyterlab": true } } }
```
  plus a parallel `jupyter-config/jupyter_notebook_config.d/jupyterlab.json`.
- Wired up by hatchling shared-data, `/Users/tel/git/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/pyproject.toml:151-157`: `"jupyter-config" = "etc/jupyter"`.
- Build backend, `pyproject.toml:4-6`: `requires = ["hatchling&gt;=1.21.1", "jupyter-builder&gt;=1.1.1"]`, `build-backend = "hatchling.build"`; the build hook is `[tool.hatch.build.hooks.jupyter-builder]` with `dependencies = ["hatch-jupyter-builder&gt;=0.3.2"]` (`:210-224`). So **hatchling + hatch-jupyter-builder + jupyter-builder**, all three.

## 5. What's new in 4.5–4.7 that affects extension authors

From `extension_migration.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`:

**4.5 → 4.6** (the consequential one):
1. **jupyter-builder split** — `extension_migration.md:30-66`, detailed above. Changelog: #18723, #18792, #18841 (removal), #18895 (`jupyter-builder` v1.0.0b1).
2. **Rspack replaces webpack** — `extension_migration.md:68-76`; changelog #16005 "Switch from `webpack` to `rspack` for bundling", then #18467 "Update to Rspack 2.0". Only affects you if you use `jupyterlab.webpackConfig`.
3. **setuptools no longer a runtime dep of JupyterLab** — `extension_migration.md:36`.
4. **Theme CSS variables** — new `--jp-datagrid-font-size`, `--jp-datagrid-font-family`, `--jp-focus-outline-color`, `--jp-focus-outline-width`; **removed** `--jp-search-toggle-{off,hover,on}-opacity` (`extension_migration.md:78-91`).
5. **API** — `IDebugger.Model.ISources.currentFrameChanged` deprecated (removal in 5.0); `LruCache` throws on `maxSize &lt; 1`; cell `syncEditable`/`syncCollapse`/`syncScrolled` now default to `undefined` not `false`; **`@jupyter/ydoc` bumped to v4** (dirty state now set on every change except `setSource()`) (`extension_migration.md:93-100`).
6. **Galata** — `runCell()` gains an options arg; `autoGoto` now resets the workspace by default (opt out with `resetWorkspace: false`); `waitForCondition()` default timeout now 15s (`extension_migration.md:102-111`).

**4.5.0 → 4.5.1**: `IDefaultContentProvider` token "was wrongfully made public", now deprecated, removal in 5.0 (`extension_migration.md:113-117`).

**4.4 → 4.5**: `DirListing` subclasses should emit the new `selectionChanged` signal; `NbConvertManager.IExportFormats` → `NbConvert.IExportFormats`; `renameDialog` deprecated in favor of `DocumentManagerDialogs.rename`; default labextension paths now take precedence over `extra_labextensions_path` (`extension_migration.md:119-142`).

**4.6 → 4.7 (unreleased)**: only one entry — **xterm.js 5.x → 6.x** (`extension_migration.md:9-26`). `@xterm/addon-canvas` removed upstream so the terminal may have no `&lt;canvas&gt;`; the search addon dropped the `xterm-find-active-result-decoration` class; `.xterm-viewport` is now a custom scrollable element; extensions typing against `Terminal.searchAddon` must bump their own `@xterm/*` deps.

Nothing about ESM/module-format changes for extensions in 4.5–4.7. The relevant statement is still the old one at `extension_dev.md:786`: "The package should export EMCAScript 6 compatible JavaScript", and for pre-bundling, `output.library.type` must be `"commonjs2"` (`:806-809`).

Also new-ish and useful: **`ServiceManagerPlugin`** for swapping out service-manager-level services (custom `IContentsManager`, etc.) — `extension_dev.md:214-288`, with the warning at `:285-289` that its `activate` receives `null` as its first arg rather than the app.

## 6. Plugin shape (`extension_points.md` / `extension_dev.md`)

`extension_points.md` itself contains no plugin-object definition — it opens straight into core tokens (`:26-34`, `:36-44`, both `{include}`-generated lists) and then extension points. The canonical shape is in `extension_dev.md:98-110`:

```typescript
const plugin: JupyterFrontEndPlugin&lt;MyToken&gt; = {
  id: 'my-extension:plugin',
  description: 'Provides a new service.',
  autoStart: true,
  requires: [ILabShell, ITranslator],
  optional: [ICommandPalette],
  provides: MyToken,
  activate: activateFunction
};
```

Only `id` and `activate` are required (`:112`). The `id` convention is load-bearing (`:116-126`):
&gt; The convention is to use the NPM extension package name, a colon, then a string identifying the plugin inside the extension, for example `my-extension:plugin`. JupyterLab treats the part before the first colon as the extension name when applying extension-level configuration such as enabling, disabling, deferring, or locking all plugins in that extension.

The same `&lt;pkg&gt;:&lt;name&gt;` convention drives settings-schema lookup (`extension_dev.md:352`). There's an eslint rule for the token variant: `jupyter/token-format` from `@jupyter/eslint-plugin` (`:124-126`). Field-by-field docs at `:127-135`; `deactivate` is optional (`:135`).

- `/Users/tel/git/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/_version.py:9` → `VersionInfo(4, 7, 0, "alpha", 1)`, i.e. `__version__ == "4.7.0a1"`.

## Practical upshot for a new frontend+server extension against this tree

The docs give you: copier template → `pip install -ve .` → `jupyter-builder develop --overwrite .` → `jlpm watch`. Your `pyproject.toml` wants `requires = ["hatchling&gt;=1.21.1", "hatch-nodejs-version&gt;=0.3.2", "jupyter-builder&gt;=1.0.0"]` with a `[tool.hatch.build.hooks.jupyter-builder]` section and a `shared-data` mapping of both `&lt;pypkg&gt;/labextension` → `share/jupyter/labextensions/&lt;js-name&gt;` and `jupyter-config` → `etc/jupyter`. Your `package.json` wants `"@jupyter/builder": "^1.0.0"` (never `@jupyterlab/builder`, which no longer exists) plus `jupyterlab: { extension: true, outputDir: "&lt;pypkg&gt;/labextension" }` and `schemaDir: "schema"` if you ship settings. The server side you'll have to take from the template, since these docs never describe it.</result>
````

````
Every one of these checkouts is frozen in 2021 or earlier, in the JupyterLab 3.0/3.1 era. **None of them uses hatchling, hatch-jupyter-builder, a `[project]` table, `[tool.hatch.build.hooks.jupyter-builder]`, or `shared-data`** — those didn't exist yet. So: treat the *packaging* layer in these repos as dead and take it from the modern template; take only the *structural and stylistic* conventions from Max. Details below, then a distilled diff list at the end.

---

## 1. jupyter-fs — `/Users/tel/git/jupyter-fs`
The most representative "Max does a full-stack extension" repo, and the only one whose TS side he designed from scratch in the JLab 3 era.

**Git.** Remotes: `origin` = `git@github.com:telamonian/jupyter-fs.git`, `upstream` = `jpmorganchase/jupyter-fs`, plus `lsowen` and `timkpaine`. Default branch `origin/master`. **HEAD is detached-ish on `release-v0.3.1` tracking `upstream/release-v0.3.1`**, last commit `2021-06-03 20:53:46 -0400 8657051 Bump version: 0.3.0final0 → 0.3.1final0`. Fetched Jun 2021. Note `origin/master` (his fork) is even older, Nov 2020.

**Idiosyncrasy #1 — the frontend lives in `js/`, not at the repo root.** Root `/Users/tel/git/jupyter-fs/package.json` is a 6-line private yarn-workspaces shim (`"workspaces": ["js"]`) with only `develop` and `test:browser` scripts. The real npm package is `/Users/tel/git/jupyter-fs/js/package.json`. This is the single biggest divergence from the official template, which puts `src/`, `package.json`, and `tsconfig.json` at the root alongside the Python package.

**pyproject.toml** (`/Users/tel/git/jupyter-fs/pyproject.toml`) is 10 lines — build-system only, plus a `[tool.pyright]` block with `venv = "jup-test"`. No project metadata:
```
requires = ["jupyter_packaging~=0.7.9", "jupyterlab&gt;=3.0.0rc13,==3.*", "setuptools&gt;=40.8.0", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"
```
All real metadata is in `/Users/tel/git/jupyter-fs/setup.py`: `install_requires` = fs, fs-s3fs, fs.smbfs, jupyterlab&gt;=3.0.0, jupyter_server&gt;=1.8.0; `extras_require={'dev': ..., 'test': ...}` where `dev = test + [autopep8, bump2version, flake8, Sphinx, sphinx-markdown-builder]` and `test = [boto3, docker, fs-miniofs, mock, pysmb, pytest, pytest-cov]`. License is **Apache 2.0** (confirmed in `LICENSE`) — note the root `package.json` says `BSD-3-Clause` and `js/package.json` says `Apache-2.0`, a live inconsistency in his repo. Flake8/pycodestyle config lives in `setup.cfg` with `max-line-length=200`, `extend-ignore=E302`.

`data_files_spec` in setup.py maps three things (this is the pre-hatch equivalent of `shared-data`): the labextension dist → `share/jupyter/labextensions/jupyter-fs`, `install.json` → same dir, and `jupyter-config/jupyter_server_config.d/jupyterfs.json` → `etc/jupyter/jupyter_server_config.d`. Build command is `install_npm(js_pkg, build_cmd='build:prod', npm=['jlpm'])` — **`jlpm`, never `npm`**.

**js/package.json.** Unscoped npm name `jupyter-fs` (not `@jupyterlab/...`). `jupyterlab` section: `extension: true`, `outputDir: "../jupyterfs/labextension"` (relative up-and-over, because of the `js/` split), `schemaDir: "schema"`, `discovery.server.managers: ["pip"]`. **No `sharedPackages`.** Scripts follow the template names (`build`, `build:prod`, `build:lib`, `build:labextension[:prod]`, `watch`/`watch:lib`/`watch:labextension`, `clean`, `clean:labextension`) plus his own additions: `clean:slate`, `deduplicate` (yarn-deduplicate `-s fewer`), `integrity` (`jlpm install &amp;&amp; jlpm deduplicate &amp;&amp; jlpm install`), `fix`, `prepack`/`postpack` using `shx` to copy the root README into the js dir for publishing, and `test:browser` → `../ci/browser_check.sh`. Every internal script call is `jlpm`, and `build:labextension` passes `--source-map=True` in **both** dev and prod.

devDeps: `@jupyterlab/builder ^3.0.0`, `typescript ^4.2.4`, `eslint ^7.0.0` + `@typescript-eslint/* ^4.26.0`, `jest ^26.6.3` + `ts-jest ^26.5.4`, `@types/jest ^26`, `rimraf ^2.7.1`, `shx`, `yarn-deduplicate`. **No prettier at all in this repo** (confirmed: no `.prettierrc`/`.prettierignore` anywhere outside node_modules). eslint plugins he adds beyond the template: `eslint-plugin-import`, `eslint-plugin-jsdoc`, `eslint-plugin-prefer-arrow`, `eslint-plugin-unicorn`, `eslint-plugin-react`. `resolutions: {"**/@types/react": "^17.0.0"}`. He also declares `@types/file-saver` and `@types/jszip` as **runtime `dependencies`**, not devDeps.

**Python layout.** Package dir `jupyterfs/` (no underscore-matching-npm-name). `/Users/tel/git/jupyter-fs/jupyterfs/__init__.py` reads `labextension/package.json` at import time and defines `_jupyter_labextension_paths()`. **The server entry point lives in a separate `jupyterfs/extension.py`**, which defines the legacy `_jupyter_server_extension_paths()` (not `_jupyter_server_extension_points()`) and `_load_jupyter_server_extension(serverapp)`. Handlers are not in a `handlers.py` — they're colocated with their managers (`metamanager.py` holds `MetaManager` + `MetaManagerHandler`; also `fsmanager.py`, `auth.py`, `config.py`, `pathutils.py`, `contents_managers/`). `jupyter-config/` has **two** files: `jupyter_server_config.d/jupyterfs.json` (enables `jupyterfs.extension`) and a top-level `jupyter_server_config.json` setting `contents_manager_class`. **No notebook v6 shim** — jupyter_server only.

**Tests.** Python tests live *inside* the package at `/Users/tel/git/jupyter-fs/jupyterfs/tests/` (`test_extension.py`, `test_fsmanager.py`, `test_init.py`, `utils/`), with a `conftest.py` that registers custom `mac`/`linux`/`windows` platform markers and auto-skips. Handler tests use `mock.MagicMock` + raw `tornado.web.Application`, **not** jupyter_server fixtures. JS tests at `/Users/tel/git/jupyter-fs/js/tests/` with `testRegex: "tests/.*\.test\.ts[x]?$"` (`.test.ts`, not `.spec.ts`), a dedicated `tsconfig.test.json` that widens `rootDir` to `.`, plus `styleMock.js`/`fileMock.js`/`assetsTransformer.js` and `jest-raw-loader` for SVGs.

**Lint/format.** `/Users/tel/git/jupyter-fs/js/.eslintrc.js` — legacy `.eslintrc.js`, ~100 explicit rules, notably **double quotes** (`"quotes": ["error", "double"]`), 2-space indent, `comma-dangle: always-multiline`, `max-len: 200`, `arrow-parens: as-needed`, `id-blacklist` banning bare `any`/`number`/`string`, and the full `recommended-requiring-type-checking` tier for `.ts`/`.tsx`. `tsconfig.json`: `target: es2019`, `jsx: react`, `composite`, `noUnusedLocals`, `noImplicitAny` — but **`strictNullChecks` is commented out** and `strict` is absent. Python side: flake8 + autopep8 (not black, not ruff), no pre-commit config.

**CI.** `.github/workflows/` contains only `binder-on-pr.yml`. Real CI is **Azure Pipelines** (`azure-pipelines.yml`, Python 3.7, Node 12.x, ubuntu-latest + macos-10.14) and **AppVeyor** (`appveyor.yml`, Windows, Python 3.7, Node 12) — he needed real SMB/S3 shares for tests, hence `ci/*.sh`/`*.ps1` scripts that provision OS shares and MinIO.

**Other.** `/Users/tel/git/jupyter-fs/Makefile` is the developer UX front door (`make dev_install`, `testjs`/`testpy`/`testbrowser`, `lint`/`fix`, `dist`, `publish`). Versioning via **bump2version** (`/Users/tel/git/jupyter-fs/.bumpversion.cfg`), with `major.minor.patch{release}{build}` ("0.3.1final0") in `jupyterfs/_version.py` and a separate npm-style serialization for `js/package.json` — i.e. **version source of truth is Python, pushed into package.json**, the opposite of the official template. `MANIFEST.in` is hand-maintained and there's a `[manifix]` section in setup.cfg. `src/` uses a single `index.tsx` holding the `JupyterFrontEndPlugin` inline (no separate `plugin.ts`); plugin id is `"jupyter-fs:plugin"`; `svg.d.ts` for SVG imports.

Notable convention he carries forward: **npm scripts drive the Python linters too** — `black:check`/`black:fix`, and `lint:check` = `eslint:check &amp;&amp; prettier:check &amp;&amp; black:check`, `lint:fix` likewise. `typescript ^3.9.0`, `eslint ^7.15.0`, `prettier ^2.2.1`, `husky ^3` + `lint-staged ^10.5.3`.

**CI.** `.github/workflows/python.yml` (name `pytest`, Python 3.6–3.9 matrix, ubuntu-latest, `pip install -e .[dev]` then `python -m pytest jupyterlab_hdf`, `timeout-minutes: 120`) and `binder-on-pr.yml`. No JS CI.

**Other.** `/Users/tel/git/jupyterlab-hdf/release.py` — a custom release script that asserts the `package.json` version equals `jupyterlab_hdf/_version.py`, then tags/pushes/publishes to both PyPI and npm, running `jlpm install` + `jlpm clean:slate` first. Plus a `.autoversion/` directory. Same pattern as jupyter-fs: **Python `_version.py` is authoritative, package.json is forced to agree.**

## Conventions that differ from the official jupyterlab/extension-template

Ordered roughly by how much they'd change your scaffold. Items marked ⚠️ are obsolete-by-vintage, not live preferences.

1. **Frontend in a `js/` subdirectory, root `package.json` is a private yarn-workspaces stub.** jupyter-fs only. Forces `outputDir: "../jupyterfs/labextension"` and `../ci/...` script paths. The template (and jupyterlab-git) put everything at the root. This is his most distinctive layout choice, and the one to make a deliberate decision about.
2. **Python `_version.py` is the version source of truth; package.json is forced to match** — via bump2version (jupyter-fs `.bumpversion.cfg`) or a custom `release.py` (jupyterlab-hdf). The modern template does the reverse (`tool.hatch.version` reading `package.json`). jupyterlab-git also does the reverse, but that's fcollonval's repo.
3. **A `Makefile` as the developer front door** (`make dev_install`, `make test`, `make lint`, `make fix`, `make dist`, `make publish`), present in jupyter-fs and jupyterlab-react-widgets. The template has no Makefile.
4. **Python linters invoked through npm scripts** — `black:check`/`black:fix` in package.json, and a combined `lint:check`/`lint:fix` spanning eslint + prettier + black (jupyterlab-hdf).
5. **`integrity` + `deduplicate` scripts** (`yarn-deduplicate -s fewer`, then reinstall) in jupyter-fs and tree-finder. Not in the template.
6. **`prepack`/`postpack` with `shx`** to copy README/LICENSE into the publishable subpackage and remove them after. jupyter-fs and tree-finder.
7. **Double quotes and a ~100-rule hand-written eslint config, with no prettier at all** in jupyter-fs — versus the template's prettier-first, single-quote setup. His other repos (hdf) *do* use prettier with single quotes, so this is inconsistent across his work; pick one. Either way he uses legacy `.eslintrc.js`, never flat `eslint.config.*`.
8. **`max-len` / `line-length` of 200** everywhere — flake8, pycodestyle, black, and eslint. Very wide.
9. **Looser TS strictness than the template**: jupyter-fs has `strictNullChecks` commented out and no `strict`; tree-finder turns `strictNullChecks` on but not full `strict`. He does consistently set `noUnusedLocals`, `noImplicitAny`, `composite`, `incremental`, `noEmitOnError`, and `target: es2019`.
10. **A local `tsconfigbase.json` that the real `tsconfig.json` extends**, plus a separate `tsconfig.eslint.json` (widened `include`) and `tsconfig.test.json` (widened `rootDir`). The template ships a single tsconfig.
11. **Server entry point in a separate `extension.py`, not `__init__.py`**, with handlers colocated with their business logic rather than a single `handlers.py` (jupyter-fs). He also uses camelCase Python filenames (`baseHandler.py`, jupyterlab-hdf).
12. **Python tests inside the package** (`jupyterfs/tests/`, `jupyterlab_hdf/tests/`) rather than a top-level `tests/`, and jupyter-fs's handler tests use `MagicMock` + bare tornado rather than jupyter_server fixtures. He also registers custom platform markers (`@pytest.mark.mac` etc.) in conftest.
13. **Jest `testRegex` uses `.test.ts`**, not the template's `.spec.ts` (jupyter-fs; jupyterlab-git uses `.spec.ts`).
14. **flake8 + autopep8, not black/ruff**, in jupyter-fs; black-only (no ruff, no mypy) in hdf and jupyterlab-git. No mypy or ruff anywhere.
15. **A hand-written `MANIFEST.in`** plus a `[manifix]` section in setup.cfg for keeping it honest. Irrelevant under hatchling, but tells you he cares about sdist contents.
16. **`jlpm` exclusively**, never bare `npm`/`yarn`, in every script and in the build hook (`npm=['jlpm']`) — this matches the template, but note tree-finder uses plain `yarn` since it's not a labextension.
17. **`binder-on-pr.yml` in `.github/workflows/`** in all three extension repos — he consistently ships a Binder demo.
18. ⚠️ **Non-GitHub-Actions CI** (Azure Pipelines + AppVeyor in jupyter-fs) for cross-platform/integration needs. Modernize this.
19. ⚠️ **jupyter_packaging 0.7 + setup.py + `create_cmdclass`/`data_files_spec`** — replace wholesale with hatchling + hatch-jupyter-builder + `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.shared-data]`.
20. ⚠️ **Notebook v6 compat via a second `jupyter_notebook_config.d/*.json`** and a `load_jupyter_server_extension = _load_jupyter_server_extension` alias (jupyterlab-git). Drop unless you need nbclassic.
21. **License: he is inconsistent** — Apache-2.0 for jupyter-fs (JPMorgan's requirement), BSD-3-Clause for everything personal (tree-finder, jupyterlab-hdf). **BSD-3-Clause is his personal default.** Never MIT. Note the jupyter-fs root `package.json` incorrectly says BSD-3-Clause while `LICENSE`/`setup.py` say Apache-2.0.
22. **`sharedPackages` only where genuinely needed** — jupyter-fs has none; jupyterlab-git's block (react/react-dom/codemirror/nbdime `bundled: false, singleton: true`) is the reference if you need it.
23. **`@types/*` sometimes declared as runtime `dependencies`** rather than devDeps (jupyter-fs: `@types/file-saver`, `@types/jszip`), plus a `resolutions` pin on `**/@types/react`.
24. **Plugin defined inline in `src/index.tsx`** with an `activate` function above it and a `"&lt;name&gt;:plugin"` id — no separate `plugin.ts`. Also a `src/svg.d.ts` shim in both jupyter-fs and jupyterlab-git.
````

````
### Settings you asked about

## 3. Repo README — the exact command and prerequisites

```sh
pip install "copier~=9.2" jinja2-time
```
or
```sh
conda install -c conda-forge "copier&gt;=9.2,&lt;10" jinja2-time
```

Then:
```sh
mkdir myextension
cd myextension
copier copy --trust https://github.com/jupyterlab/extension-template .
```

Older version: `copier copy --vcs-ref v4.0.0 --trust https://github.com/jupyterlab/extension-template .`
Update in place: `copier update --trust`

        }
    }
}
```

Note the file is indented with **4 spaces** (enforced by the prettier `package.json` override).

  optional: [ISettingRegistry],{% endif %}
  activate: (app: JupyterFrontEnd{% if kind.lower() == 'theme' %}, manager: IThemeManager{% endif %}{% if has_settings %}, settingRegistry: ISettingRegistry | null{% endif %}) =&gt; {
    console.log('JupyterLab extension {{ labextension_name }} is activated!');{% if kind.lower() == 'theme' %}
    const style = '{{ labextension_name }}/index.css';

    manager.register({
      name: '{{ labextension_name }}',
      isLight: true,
      load: () =&gt; manager.loadCSS(style),
      unload: () =&gt; Promise.resolve(undefined)
    });{% endif %}{% if has_settings %}

    if (settingRegistry) {
      settingRegistry
        .load(plugin.id)
        .then(settings =&gt; {
          console.log('{{ labextension_name }} settings loaded:', settings.composite);
        })
        .catch(reason =&gt; {
          console.error('Failed to load settings for {{ labextension_name }}.', reason);
        });
    }{% endif %}{% if kind.lower() == 'frontend-and-server' %}

    requestAPI&lt;any&gt;('hello', app.serviceManager.serverSettings)
      .then(data =&gt; {
        console.log(data);
      })
      .catch(reason =&gt; {
        console.error(
          `The {{ python_name }} server extension appears to be missing.\n${reason}`
        );
      });{% endif %}

};

export default plugin;
{% else %}import { IRenderMime } from '@jupyterlab/rendermime-interfaces';
{% if data_format == 'json' %}
import { JSONObject } from '@lumino/coreutils';
{% endif %}
import { Widget } from '@lumino/widgets';

/**
 * The default mime type for the extension.
 */
const MIME_TYPE = '{{ mimetype }}';

/**
 * The class name added to the extension.
 */
const CLASS_NAME = 'mimerenderer-{{ mimetype_name }}';

/**
 * A widget for rendering {{ mimetype_name }}.
 */
export class OutputWidget extends Widget implements IRenderMime.IRenderer {
  /**
   * Construct a new output widget.
   */
  constructor(options: IRenderMime.IRendererOptions) {
    super();
    this._mimeType = options.mimeType;
    this.addClass(CLASS_NAME);
  }

  /**
   * Render {{mimetype_name}} into this widget's node.
   */
  renderModel(model: IRenderMime.IMimeModel): Promise&lt;void&gt; {
    {% if data_format == 'json' %}const data = model.data[this._mimeType] as JSONObject;
    this.node.textContent = JSON.stringify(data);
    {% else %}const data = model.data[this._mimeType] as string;
    this.node.textContent = data.slice(0, 16384);{% endif %}
    return Promise.resolve();
  }

  private _mimeType: string;
}

/**
 * A mime renderer factory for {{ mimetype_name }} data.
 */
export const rendererFactory: IRenderMime.IRendererFactory = {
  safe: true,
  mimeTypes: [MIME_TYPE],
  createRenderer: options =&gt; new OutputWidget(options)
};

/**
 * Extension definition.
 */
const extension: IRenderMime.IExtension = {
  id: '{{labextension_name}}:plugin',
  // description: 'Adds MIME type renderer for {{ mimetype_name }} content',
  rendererFactory,
  rank: 100,
  dataType: '{{ data_format }}',
  fileTypes: [
    {
      name: '{{ mimetype_name }}',
      mimeTypes: [MIME_TYPE],
      extensions: ['{{ file_extension }}']
    }
  ],
  documentWidgetFactoryOptions: {
    name: '{{ viewer_name }}',
    primaryFileType: '{{ mimetype_name }}',
    fileTypes: ['{{ mimetype_name }}'],
    defaultFor: ['{{ mimetype_name }}']
  }
};

export default extension;
{% endif %}
```

### `template/src/{% if kind == 'frontend-and-server' %}request.ts{% endif %}.jinja` → `src/request.ts`

```jinja
import { URLExt } from '@jupyterlab/coreutils';

import { ServerConnection } from '@jupyterlab/services';

/**
 * Call the server extension
 *
 * @param endPoint API REST end point for the extension
 * @param serverSettings The server settings to use for the request
 * @param init Initial values for the request
 * @returns The response body interpreted as JSON
 */
export async function requestAPI&lt;T&gt;(
  endPoint: string,
  serverSettings: ServerConnection.ISettings,
  init: RequestInit = {}
): Promise&lt;T&gt; {
  // Make request to Jupyter API
  const requestUrl = URLExt.join(
    serverSettings.baseUrl,
    '{{ python_name | replace("_", "-") }}', // our server extension's API namespace
    endPoint
  );

  let response: Response;
  try {
    response = await ServerConnection.makeRequest(
      requestUrl,
      init,
      serverSettings
    );
  } catch (error) {
    throw new ServerConnection.NetworkError(error as any);
  }

  let data: any = await response.text();

  if (data.length &gt; 0) {
    try {
      data = JSON.parse(data);
    } catch (error) {
      console.log('Not a JSON response body.', response);
    }
  }

  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new ServerConnection.ResponseError(response, data.message || data);
  }

  return data;
}
```

### `template/{{python_name}}/{% if kind == 'frontend-and-server' %}routes.py{% endif %}.jinja` → `{{python_name}}/routes.py`

```jinja
import json

from jupyter_server.base.handlers import APIHandler
from jupyter_server.utils import url_path_join
import tornado

class HelloRouteHandler(APIHandler):
    # The following decorator should be present on all verb methods (head, get, post,
    # patch, put, delete, options) to ensure only authorized user can request the
    # Jupyter server
    @tornado.web.authenticated
    def get(self):
        self.finish(json.dumps({
            "data": (
                "Hello, world!"
                " This is the '/{{ python_name | replace('_', '-') }}/hello' endpoint."
                " Try visiting me in your browser!"
            ),
        }))


def setup_route_handlers(web_app):
    host_pattern = ".*$"
    base_url = web_app.settings["base_url"]

    hello_route_pattern = url_path_join(base_url, "{{ python_name | replace('_', '-') }}", "hello")
    handlers = [(hello_route_pattern, HelloRouteHandler)]

    web_app.add_handlers(host_pattern, handlers)
```

import { expect, test } from '@jupyterlab/galata';

{% if kind != 'mimerenderer' %}/**
 * Don't load JupyterLab webpage before running the tests.
 * This is required to ensure we capture all log messages.
 */
test.use({ autoGoto: false });

test('should emit an activation console message', async ({ page }) =&gt; {
  const logs: string[] = [];

  page.on('console', message =&gt; {
    logs.push(message.text());
  });

  await page.goto();

  expect(
    logs.filter(s =&gt; s === 'JupyterLab extension {{ labextension_name }} is activated!')
  ).toHaveLength(1);
});
{% else %}test('should display {{ mimetype_name }} data file', async ({ page }) =&gt; {
  const filename = 'test{{ file_extension }}';
  await page.menu.clickMenuItem('File&gt;New&gt;Text File');

  // Set MIME type content in fill
  await page.getByRole('main').getByRole('textbox').fill('');

  await page.menu.clickMenuItem('File&gt;Save Text');

  await page.locator('.jp-Dialog').getByRole('textbox').fill(filename);

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Rename' }).click();
  await page.waitForTimeout(200);

  // Close file opened as editor
  await page.activity.closePanel('test.my_type');

  await page.filebrowser.open(filename);

  const view = page.getByRole('main').locator('.mimerenderer-{{ mimetype_name }}');

  expect(await view.screenshot()).toMatchSnapshot('{{ mimetype_name }}-file.png');
});

test('should display notebook {{ mimetype_name }} output', async ({ page }) =&gt; {
  await page.menu.clickMenuItem('File&gt;New&gt;Notebook');

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Select' }).click();

  await page.notebook.setCell(
    0,
    'code',
    `from IPython.display import display
# Example of MIME type content
output = {
    "{{ mimetype }}": ""
}

display(output, raw=True)`
  );

  await page.notebook.run();

  const outputs = page
    .getByRole('main')
    .locator('.mimerenderer-{{ mimetype_name }}.jp-OutputArea-output');

  await expect(outputs).toHaveCount(1);
});
{% endif %}
```

### `template/{% if test %}ui-tests{% endif %}/README.md`

```markdown
# Integration Testing

This folder contains the integration tests of the extension.

They are defined using [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro) test runner
and [Galata](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/tree/main/galata) helper.

The Playwright configuration is defined in [playwright.config.js](./playwright.config.js).

The JupyterLab server configuration to use for the integration test is defined
in [jupyter_server_test_config.py](./jupyter_server_test_config.py).

The default configuration will produce video for failing tests and an HTML report.

&gt; There is a UI mode that you may like; see [that video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jF0yA-JLQW0).

## Run the tests

&gt; All commands are assumed to be executed from the root directory

To run the tests, you need to:

1. Compile the extension:

```sh
jlpm install
jlpm build:prod
```

&gt; Check the extension is installed in JupyterLab.

2. Install test dependencies (needed only once):

```sh
cd ./ui-tests
jlpm install
jlpm playwright install
cd ..
```

3. Execute the [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro) tests:

```sh
cd ./ui-tests
jlpm playwright test
```

Test results will be shown in the terminal. In case of any test failures, the test report
will be opened in your browser at the end of the tests execution; see
[Playwright documentation](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-reporters#html-reporter)
for configuring that behavior.

## Update the tests snapshots

&gt; All commands are assumed to be executed from the root directory

If you are comparing snapshots to validate your tests, you may need to update
the reference snapshots stored in the repository. To do that, you need to:

1. Compile the extension:

```sh
jlpm install
jlpm build:prod
```

&gt; Check the extension is installed in JupyterLab.

2. Install test dependencies (needed only once):

```sh
cd ./ui-tests
jlpm install
jlpm playwright install
cd ..
```

3. Execute the [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro) command:

```sh
cd ./ui-tests
jlpm playwright test -u
```

&gt; Some discrepancy may occurs between the snapshots generated on your computer and
&gt; the one generated on the CI. To ease updating the snapshots on a PR, you can
&gt; type `please update playwright snapshots` to trigger the update by a bot on the CI.
&gt; Once the bot has computed new snapshots, it will commit them to the PR branch.

## Create tests

&gt; All commands are assumed to be executed from the root directory

To create tests, the easiest way is to use the code generator tool of playwright:

1. Compile the extension:

```sh
jlpm install
jlpm build:prod
```

&gt; Check the extension is installed in JupyterLab.

2. Install test dependencies (needed only once):

```sh
cd ./ui-tests
jlpm install
jlpm playwright install
cd ..
```

3. Start the server:

```sh
cd ./ui-tests
jlpm start
```

4. Execute the [Playwright code generator](https://playwright.dev/docs/codegen) in **another terminal**:

```sh
cd ./ui-tests
jlpm playwright codegen localhost:8888
```

## Debug tests

&gt; All commands are assumed to be executed from the root directory

To debug tests, a good way is to use the inspector tool of playwright:

1. Compile the extension:

```sh
jlpm install
jlpm build:prod
```

&gt; Check the extension is installed in JupyterLab.

2. Install test dependencies (needed only once):

```sh
cd ./ui-tests
jlpm install
jlpm playwright install
cd ..
```

3. Execute the Playwright tests in [debug mode](https://playwright.dev/docs/debug):

```sh
cd ./ui-tests
jlpm playwright test --debug
```

## Upgrade Playwright and the browsers

To update the web browser versions, you must update the package `@playwright/test`:

```sh
cd ./ui-tests
jlpm up "@playwright/test"
jlpm playwright install
```
```

### `template/.github/workflows/build.yml.jinja`

```jinja
name: Build

on:
  push:
    branches: main
  pull_request:
    branches: '*'
{% raw %}
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
{% endraw %}
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Checkout
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Base Setup
      uses: jupyterlab/maintainer-tools/.github/actions/base-setup@v1

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: python -m pip install -U "jupyterlab&gt;=4.0.0,&lt;5"

    - name: Lint the extension
      run: |
        set -eux
        jlpm
        jlpm run lint:check
{% if test %}
    - name: Test the extension
      run: |
        set -eux
        jlpm run test
{% endif %}
    - name: Build the extension
      run: |
        set -eux
        python -m pip install .[test]
{% if kind.lower() == 'frontend-and-server' %}{% if test %}
        pytest -vv -r ap --cov {{ python_name }}{% endif %}
        jupyter server extension list
        jupyter server extension list 2&gt;&amp;1 | grep -ie "{{ python_name }}.*OK"
{% endif %}
        jupyter labextension list
        jupyter labextension list 2&gt;&amp;1 | grep -ie "{{ labextension_name }}.*OK"
        python -m jupyterlab.browser_check
{% if kind.lower() == 'frontend-and-server' %}
    - name: Check that all endpoints are authenticated
      run: |
        set -eux
        python .github/scripts/check_auth.py
{% endif %}
    - name: Package the extension
      run: |
        set -eux

        pip install build
        python -m build
        pip uninstall -y "{{ python_name }}" jupyterlab

    - name: Upload extension packages
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: extension-artifacts
        path: dist/{{ python_name }}*
        if-no-files-found: error

  test_isolated:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - name: Install Python
      uses: actions/setup-python@v5
      with:
        python-version: '3.10'
        architecture: 'x64'
    - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: extension-artifacts
    - name: Install and Test
      run: |
        set -eux
        # Remove NodeJS, twice to take care of system and locally installed node versions.
        sudo rm -rf $(which node)
        sudo rm -rf $(which node)

        pip install "jupyterlab&gt;=4.0.0,&lt;5" {{ python_name }}*.whl

{% if kind.lower() == 'frontend-and-server' %}
        jupyter server extension list
        jupyter server extension list 2&gt;&amp;1 | grep -ie "{{ python_name }}.*OK"
{% endif %}
        jupyter labextension list
        jupyter labextension list 2&gt;&amp;1 | grep -ie "{{ labextension_name }}.*OK"
        python -m jupyterlab.browser_check --no-browser-test
{% if test %}
  integration-tests:
    name: Integration tests
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    env:
      PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH: ${{ "{{ github.workspace }}" }}/pw-browsers

    steps:
    - name: Checkout
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Base Setup
      uses: jupyterlab/maintainer-tools/.github/actions/base-setup@v1

    - name: Download extension package
      uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: extension-artifacts

    - name: Install the extension
      run: |
        set -eux
        python -m pip install "jupyterlab&gt;=4.0.0,&lt;5" {{ python_name }}*.whl

    - name: Install dependencies
      working-directory: ui-tests
      env:
        YARN_ENABLE_IMMUTABLE_INSTALLS: 0
        PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD: 1
      run: jlpm install
{% raw %}
    - name: Set up browser cache
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: |
          ${{ github.workspace }}/pw-browsers
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('ui-tests/yarn.lock') }}
{% endraw %}
    - name: Install browser
      run: |
        set -eux
        jlpm playwright install chromium --only-shell
      working-directory: ui-tests

    - name: Execute integration tests
      working-directory: ui-tests
      run: |
        jlpm playwright test

    - name: Upload Playwright Test report
      if: always()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: {{ python_name }}-playwright-tests
        path: |
          ui-tests/test-results
          ui-tests/playwright-report{% endif %}

  check_links:
    name: Check Links
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: jupyterlab/maintainer-tools/.github/actions/base-setup@v1
      - uses: jupyterlab/maintainer-tools/.github/actions/check-links@v1
```

### `template/.github/{% if kind == 'frontend-and-server' %}scripts{% endif %}/check_auth.py.jinja`

```jinja
"""Check that all endpoints of the extension require authentication.

When unauthenticated access is not allowed, Jupyter Server warns about every
handler which is missing an authentication decorator; this script turns such a
warning into a failure, so that no endpoint can be exposed to unauthorized users
by mistake.

Run it with:

    python .github/scripts/check_auth.py
"""
import sys
import warnings

from jupyter_server.serverapp import ServerApp
from jupyter_server.utils import JupyterServerAuthWarning

# Initialize a server which only loads this extension and which does not allow
# unauthenticated access.
app = ServerApp(
    allow_unauthenticated_access=False,
    jpserver_extensions={"{{ python_name }}": True},
    # Fail loudly if the extension cannot be loaded at all, instead of silently
    # reporting that there is nothing to complain about.
    reraise_server_extension_failures=True,
)

with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as records:
    warnings.simplefilter("always")
    app.initialize(argv=[], find_extensions=False, new_httpserver=False)

problems = [
    str(record.message)
    for record in records
    if issubclass(record.category, JupyterServerAuthWarning)
]

if problems:
    sys.exit(
        "\n".join(problems)
        + "\n\nAdd a `@tornado.web.authenticated` decorator to the verb methods listed"
        " above. If an endpoint is intended to be public, add an explicit"
        " `@allow_unauthenticated` (or `@ws_authenticated` for websockets) decorator"
        " from `jupyter_server.auth.decorator` instead."
    )

print("All endpoints of the extension require authentication.")
```

`template/.github/workflows/prep-release.yml`
```yaml
name: "Step 1: Prep Release"
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version_spec:
        description: "New Version Specifier"
        default: "next"
        required: false
      branch:
        description: "The branch to target"
        required: false
      post_version_spec:
        description: "Post Version Specifier"
        required: false
      # silent:
      #   description: "Set a placeholder in the changelog and don't publish the release."
      #   required: false
      #   type: boolean
      since:
        description: "Use PRs with activity since this date or git reference"
        required: false
      since_last_stable:
        description: "Use PRs with activity since the last stable git tag"
        required: false
        type: boolean
jobs:
  prep_release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: jupyterlab/maintainer-tools/.github/actions/base-setup@v1

      - name: Prep Release
        id: prep-release
        uses: jupyter-server/jupyter_releaser/.github/actions/prep-release@v2
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          version_spec: ${{ github.event.inputs.version_spec }}
          # silent: ${{ github.event.inputs.silent }}
          post_version_spec: ${{ github.event.inputs.post_version_spec }}
          branch: ${{ github.event.inputs.branch }}
          since: ${{ github.event.inputs.since }}
          since_last_stable: ${{ github.event.inputs.since_last_stable }}

      - name: "** Next Step **"
        run: |
          echo "Optional): Review Draft Release: ${{ steps.prep-release.outputs.release_url }}"
```

`template/.github/workflows/publish-release.yml`
```yaml
name: "Step 2: Publish Release"
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      branch:
        description: "The target branch"
        required: false
      release_url:
        description: "The URL of the draft GitHub release"
        required: false
      steps_to_skip:
        description: "Comma separated list of steps to skip"
        required: false

jobs:
  publish_release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: release
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: jupyterlab/maintainer-tools/.github/actions/base-setup@v1

      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v1
        id: app-token
        with:
          app-id: ${{ vars.APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - name: Populate Release
        id: populate-release
        uses: jupyter-server/jupyter_releaser/.github/actions/populate-release@v2
        with:
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          branch: ${{ github.event.inputs.branch }}
          release_url: ${{ github.event.inputs.release_url }}
          steps_to_skip: ${{ github.event.inputs.steps_to_skip }}

      - name: Finalize Release
        id: finalize-release
        env:
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        uses: jupyter-server/jupyter_releaser/.github/actions/finalize-release@v2
        with:
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
          release_url: ${{ steps.populate-release.outputs.release_url }}

      - name: "** Next Step **"
        if: ${{ success() }}
        run: |
          echo "Verify the final release"
          echo ${{ steps.finalize-release.outputs.release_url }}

      - name: "** Failure Message **"
        if: ${{ failure() }}
        run: |
          echo "Failed to Publish the Draft Release Url:"
          echo ${{ steps.populate-release.outputs.release_url }}
```

`template/{% if has_binder %}binder{% endif %}/postBuild.jinja`
```jinja
#!/usr/bin/env python3
""" perform a development install of {{ python_name }}

    On Binder, this will run _after_ the environment has been fully created from
    the environment.yml in this directory.

    This script should also run locally on Linux/MacOS/Windows:

        python3 binder/postBuild
"""
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path


ROOT = Path.cwd()

def _(*args, **kwargs):
    """ Run a command, echoing the args

        fails hard if something goes wrong
    """
    print("\n\t", " ".join(args), "\n")
    return_code = subprocess.call(args, **kwargs)
    if return_code != 0:
        print("\nERROR", return_code, " ".join(args))
        sys.exit(return_code)

# verify the environment is self-consistent before even starting
_(sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "check")

# install the labextension
_(sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-e", ".")
_(sys.executable, "-m", "jupyter", "labextension", "develop", "--overwrite", "."){% if kind.lower() == 'frontend-and-server' %}
_(
    sys.executable,
    "-m",
    "jupyter",
    "server",
    "extension",
    "enable",
    "{{ python_name }}",
){% endif %}

# verify the environment the extension didn't break anything
_(sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "check")

# list the extensions
_("jupyter", "server", "extension", "list")

# initially list installed extensions to determine if there are any surprises
_("jupyter", "labextension", "list")


print("JupyterLab with {{ python_name }} is ready to run with:\n")
print("\tjupyter lab\n")
```

Note `postBuild` still uses the older `jupyter labextension develop` here, unlike `CONTRIBUTING.md` which uses `jupyter-builder develop`.

### `template/LICENSE.jinja` — license choice

There is **no license question**. The template hardcodes **BSD 3-Clause** (`"license": "BSD-3-Clause"` in `package.json`, `license = "BSD-3-Clause"` + `license-files = ["LICENSE"]` in `pyproject.toml`). The file is the standard BSD-3-Clause text, 1542 bytes; only the header is templated:

```jinja
BSD 3-Clause License

Copyright (c) {% now 'utc', '%Y' %}, {{ author_name }}
All rights reserved.

Redistribution and use in source and binary forms, with or without
modification, are permitted provided that the following conditions are met:

1. Redistributions of source code must retain the above copyright notice, this
   list of conditions and the following disclaimer.

2. Redistributions in binary form must reproduce the above copyright notice,
...
```

(rest is verbatim standard BSD-3-Clause boilerplate; `{% now 'utc', '%Y' %}` is why `jinja2-time` is a prerequisite)

### `template/README.md.jinja`

```jinja
# {{ python_name }}

[![Github Actions Status]({{ repository|trim('/') }}/workflows/Build/badge.svg)]({{ repository|trim('/') }}/actions/workflows/build.yml)
{% if has_binder -%}
[![Binder](https://mybinder.org/badge_logo.svg)](https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/{{ repository|replace("https://github.com/", "") }}/main?urlpath=lab)

{% endif %}
{{ project_short_description }}
{% if kind.lower() == 'frontend-and-server' %}
This extension is composed of a Python package named `{{ python_name }}`
for the server extension and a NPM package named `{{ labextension_name }}`
for the frontend extension.
{% endif %}
## Requirements

- JupyterLab &gt;= 4.0.0

## Install

To install the extension, execute:

```bash
pip install {{ python_name }}
```

## Uninstall

To remove the extension, execute:

```bash
pip uninstall {{ python_name }}
```
{% if kind.lower() == 'frontend-and-server' %}
## Troubleshoot

If you are seeing the frontend extension, but it is not working, check
that the server extension is enabled:

```bash
jupyter server extension list
```

If the server extension is installed and enabled, but you are not seeing
the frontend extension, check the frontend extension is installed:

```bash
jupyter labextension list
```
{% endif %}
## Contributing

If you would like to contribute to this extension, please refer to the [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md).
{%- if has_ai_rules %}

## AI Coding Assistant Support

This project includes an `AGENTS.md` file with coding standards and best practices for JupyterLab extension development. The file follows the [AGENTS.md standard](https://agents.md) for cross-tool compatibility.

### Compatible AI Tools

`AGENTS.md` works with AI coding assistants that support the standard, including Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Aider, and others. For a current list of compatible tools, see [the AGENTS.md standard](https://agents.md).

{%- if create_claude_symlink or create_gemini_symlink %}
This project also includes symlinks for tool-specific compatibility:
{%- if create_claude_symlink %}

- `CLAUDE.md` → `AGENTS.md` (for Claude Code)
{%- endif %}
{%- if create_gemini_symlink %}

- `GEMINI.md` → `AGENTS.md` (for Gemini Code Assist)
{%- endif %}
{%- endif %}

Other conventions you might encounter:

- `.cursorrules` - Cursor's YAML/JSON format (Cursor also supports AGENTS.md natively)
- `CONVENTIONS.md` / `CONTRIBUTING.md` - For CodeConventions.ai and GitHub bots
- Project-specific rules in JetBrains AI Assistant settings

All tool-specific files should be symlinks to `AGENTS.md` as the single source of truth.

### What's Included

The `AGENTS.md` file provides guidance on:

- Code quality rules and file-scoped validation commands
- Naming conventions for packages, plugins, and files
- Coding standards (TypeScript{% if kind.lower() == 'frontend-and-server' %}, Python{% endif %})
- Development workflow and debugging{% if kind.lower() == 'frontend-and-server' %}
- Backend-frontend integration patterns (`APIHandler`, `requestAPI()`, routing){% endif %}{% if kind.lower() == 'theme' %}
- Theme-specific patterns (CSS organization, light/dark modes, `IThemeManager`){% endif %}{% if kind.lower() == 'mimerender' %}
- Renderer implementation (`IRenderMime.IExtension`, security, performance){% endif %}
- Common pitfalls and how to avoid them

### Customization

You can edit `AGENTS.md` to add project-specific conventions or adjust guidelines to match your team's practices. The file uses plain Markdown with Do/Don't patterns and references to actual project files.

**Note**: `AGENTS.md` is living documentation. Update it when you change conventions, add dependencies, or discover new patterns. Include `AGENTS.md` updates in commits that modify workflows or coding standards.
{%- endif %}

### `template/CONTRIBUTING.md.jinja`

This holds the dev-install instructions that used to live in `README.md` — you'll want it.

```jinja
# Contributing

## Development install

Note: You will need Node.js to build the extension package.
You may install it from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/en/download). We
recommend using the latest LTS version of Node.js.

The `jlpm` command is JupyterLab's pinned version of
[yarn](https://yarnpkg.com/) that is installed with JupyterLab. You may use
`yarn` or `npm` in lieu of `jlpm` below.

```bash
# Clone the repo to your local environment
# Change directory to the {{ python_name }} directory

# Set up a virtual environment and install package in development mode
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install --editable ".{% if test and kind.lower() == 'frontend-and-server' %}[dev,test]{% endif %}"

# Link your development version of the extension with JupyterLab
jupyter-builder develop . --overwrite{% if kind.lower() == 'frontend-and-server' %}
# Server extension must be manually installed in develop mode
jupyter server extension enable {{ python_name }}{% endif %}

# Rebuild extension Typescript source after making changes
# IMPORTANT: Unlike the steps above which are performed only once, do this step
# every time you make a change.
jlpm build
```

You can watch the source directory and run JupyterLab at the same time in different terminals to watch for changes in the extension's source and automatically rebuild the extension.

```bash
# Watch the source directory in one terminal, automatically rebuilding when needed
jlpm watch
# Run JupyterLab in another terminal
jupyter lab
```

With the watch command running, every saved change will immediately be built locally and available in your running JupyterLab. Refresh JupyterLab to load the change in your browser (you may need to wait several seconds for the extension to be rebuilt).

By default, the `jlpm build` command generates the source maps for this extension to make it easier to debug using the browser dev tools. To also generate source maps for the JupyterLab core extensions, you can run the following command:

```bash
jupyter lab build --minimize=False
```

## Development uninstall

```bash{% if kind.lower() == 'frontend-and-server' %}
# Server extension must be manually disabled in develop mode
jupyter server extension disable {{ python_name }}{% endif %}
pip uninstall {{ python_name }}
```

In development mode, you will also need to remove the symlink created by `jupyter-builder develop`
command. To find its location, you can run `jupyter labextension list` to figure out where the `labextensions`
folder is located. Then you can remove the symlink named `{{ labextension_name }}` within that folder.
{%- if kind.lower() == 'frontend-and-server' %}

## Endpoint authentication

Every verb method of every handler must carry a `@tornado.web.authenticated`
decorator, or, if the endpoint is meant to be public, an explicit
`@allow_unauthenticated`/`@ws_authenticated` decorator from
`jupyter_server.auth.decorator`. The `build` workflow enforces this by running:

```sh
python .github/scripts/check_auth.py
```
{%- endif %}
{%- if test %}

## Testing the extension{% if kind.lower() == 'frontend-and-server' %}

### Server tests

This extension is using [Pytest](https://docs.pytest.org/) for Python code testing.

Install test dependencies (needed only once):

```sh
pip install -e ".[test]"
# Each time you install the Python package, you need to restore the front-end extension link
jupyter-builder develop . --overwrite
```

To execute them, run:

```sh
pytest -vv -r ap --cov {{ python_name }}
```{% endif %}

#### Frontend tests

This extension is using [Jest](https://jestjs.io/) for JavaScript code testing.

To execute them, execute:

```sh
jlpm
jlpm test
```

### Integration tests

This extension uses [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/docs/intro) for the integration tests (aka user level tests).
More precisely, the JupyterLab helper [Galata](https://github.com/jupyterlab/jupyterlab/tree/master/galata) is used to handle testing the extension in JupyterLab.

More information is provided within the [ui-tests](./ui-tests/README.md) README.

```jinja
# Making a new release of {{ python_name }}

The extension can be published to `PyPI` and `npm` manually or using the [Jupyter Releaser](https://github.com/jupyter-server/jupyter_releaser).

## Manual release

### Python package

This extension can be distributed as Python packages. All of the Python
packaging instructions are in the `pyproject.toml` file to wrap your extension in a
Python package. Before generating a package, you first need to install some tools:

```bash
pip install build twine hatch
```

Bump the version using `hatch`. By default this will create a tag.
See the docs on [hatch-nodejs-version](https://github.com/agoose77/hatch-nodejs-version#semver) for details.

```bash
hatch version &lt;new-version&gt;
```

Make sure to clean up all the development files before building the package:

```bash
jlpm clean:all
```

You could also clean up the local git repository:

```bash
git clean -dfX
```

To create a Python source package (`.tar.gz`) and the binary package (`.whl`) in the `dist/` directory, do:

```bash
python -m build
```

&gt; `python setup.py sdist bdist_wheel` is deprecated and will not work for this package.

Then to upload the package to PyPI, do:

```bash
twine upload dist/*
```

### NPM package

To publish the frontend part of the extension as a NPM package, do:

```bash
npm login
npm publish --access public
```

## Automated releases with the Jupyter Releaser

The extension repository should already be compatible with the Jupyter Releaser. But
the GitHub repository and the package managers need to be properly set up. Please
follow the instructions of the Jupyter Releaser [checklist](https://jupyter-releaser.readthedocs.io/en/latest/how_to_guides/convert_repo_from_repo.html).

For the release workflows in this repository, make sure GitHub is configured with:

- a `release` environment
- an `APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secret
- an `APP_ID` repository variable

When using [npm trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers), `NPM_TOKEN` is not required (and trusted publishing is recommended). Configure `NPM_TOKEN` only if you are publishing without trusted publishers.

Here is a summary of the steps to cut a new release:

- Go to the Actions panel
- Run the "Step 1: Prep Release" workflow
- Check the draft changelog
- Run the "Step 2: Publish Release" workflow

&gt; [!NOTE]
&gt; Check out the [workflow documentation](https://jupyter-releaser.readthedocs.io/en/latest/get_started/making_release_from_repo.html)
&gt; for more information.

## Publishing to `conda-forge`

If the package is not on conda forge yet, check the documentation to learn how to add it: https://conda-forge.org/docs/maintainer/adding_pkgs.html

Otherwise a bot should pick up the new version publish to PyPI, and open a new PR on the feedstock repository automatically.
```

## 7. Gotchas for hand-reproduction

1. **`ui-tests/yarn.lock` is a committed empty (0-byte) file.** The CI cache key hashes it. Create it empty.
2. **`package.json` uses 4-space indent**; everything else is 2-space. The prettier override enforces this.
3. **`src/request.ts`'s `requestAPI` takes `serverSettings` as its second positional argument**, and `src/index.ts` passes `app.serviceManager.serverSettings`. This differs from every older tutorial that used `ServerConnection.makeSettings()` internally.
4. The API namespace is `python_name` with underscores replaced by hyphens — e.g. `jupyter_dag` → route prefix `/jupyter-dag/hello`.
5. **`conftest.py` lives at the repo root**, not inside the tests package, and sets `allow_unauthenticated_access: False` so missing `@tornado.web.authenticated` decorators fail tests.
6. `check_auth.py` in `.github/scripts/` is a CI gate for endpoint auth — new since older templates.
7. `build.yml` line `python -m pip install .[test]` runs unconditionally even when `test=false`; the `[test]` extra only exists for `test and frontend-and-server`. Harmless with pip for existing projects but worth knowing.
8. `.github/workflows/check-release.yml.jinja` uses `${{ '{{ github.run_number }}' }}` (a Jinja string literal) rather than `{% raw %}` for that one expression — an inconsistency in the template, renders to `${{ github.run_number }}`.
9. `enforce-label.yml`, `prep-release.yml`, `publish-release.yml`, `update-integration-tests.yml`, `binder-on-pr.yml`, `ui-tests/playwright.config.js`, `ui-tests/jupyter_server_test_config.py`, `ui-tests/README.md`, `jest.config.js`, `babel.config.js`, `tsconfig.test.json`, `style/base.css`, `style/index.js`, `CHANGELOG.md` have **no `.jinja` suffix** — copied verbatim, `${{ }}` untouched.
10. `binder/postBuild` still uses the deprecated `jupyter labextension develop`, while `CONTRIBUTING.md` uses `jupyter-builder develop`. If you're reproducing, prefer the latter.
11. `jupyterlab.discovery.server.base.name` in `package.json` is the `python_name`, and `jupyterlab.outputDir` is `{{python_name}}/labextension`.</result>
````

````
This guide provides coding standards and best practices for developing JupyterLab extensions. Follow these rules to align with community standards and keep your extension maintainable.

**Extension type**: {{ kind }}

### PRIORITY RESOURCE USAGE

**When you encounter uncertainty, incomplete information, or need implementation examples, you MUST consult these external resources FIRST before attempting to implement features.**

Use your available tools (web search, documentation search) to access and retrieve content from these resources when:

- You're unsure about API usage, method signatures, or interface requirements
- You need to verify the correct approach for a feature or pattern
````

````
a scaffold that installs, builds, and loads in the local JupyterLab 4.7.0a1 fork,
ready for the DAG view and the kernel-side work to be added later. Nothing DAG-specific
(React Flow, react, comm targets) goes in yet.

  `jupyter-config/server-config/jupyter_dag.json`, root `conftest.py`,
  `jupyter_dag/tests/test_routes.py`, jest + `src/__tests__/`, `ui-tests/` (playwright +
  galata; `ui-tests/yarn.lock` is a committed empty file), `.github/workflows/`
  (build, check-release, enforce-label, prep-release, publish-release,
  update-integration-tests, binder-on-pr), `.github/scripts/check_auth.py`,
  `binder/`, `AGENTS.md`, README/CONTRIBUTING/RELEASE/CHANGELOG/LICENSE (BSD-3-Clause),
  `.copier-answers.yml`, `.gitignore`, `.prettierignore`, `.yarnrc.yml`.
- Build tooling moved out of JupyterLab in 4.6: PyPI `jupyter-builder` (1.2.3 in the
  venv) and npm `@jupyter/builder` (1.2.3, Rspack, bundles `@jupyterlab/core-meta`
  ^4.6.1, needs Node ^20.19 || >=22.12; local Node is 26.7). `@jupyterlab/builder` no
  longer exists in 4.7. `jupyter labextension develop|build|watch` are deprecated shims
  that exec `jupyter-builder ...` from PATH (fork `jupyterlab/labextensions.py:471-483`),
  so the venv `bin/` must be on PATH.

  editable from `~/git/jupyterlab/jupyterlab` with dev static build present,
  jupyter-builder 1.2.3, hatchling 1.32, pytest-jupyter 0.11, jlpm). `copier` is not
  installed anywhere; `uvx` is available. `hatch-nodejs-version`, `hatch-jupyter-builder`,
  `pytest-asyncio` are not in the venv and will be fetched at install time.
- Names are free: npm `@telamonian/jupyter-dag`, PyPI `jupyter-dag`/`jupyter_dag`;
  no GitHub repo `telamonian/jupyter-dag` yet. git identity is `telamonian` /

  is obsolete, so the template's layout wins. Kept from his habits: BSD-3-Clause, `jlpm`
  everywhere, Binder-on-PR.

## Answers Max gave (Sept 16)

| copier question | answer |
|---|---|
| kind | `frontend-and-server` |
| author_name / author_email | `Max Klein` / `telamonian@users.noreply.github.com` |
| labextension_name / python_name | `@telamonian/jupyter-dag` / `jupyter_dag` |
| project_short_description | `Organize notebook cells into DAGs and run them reactively in JupyterLab` |
| has_settings / test / has_binder | yes / yes / yes |
| has_ai_rules | yes, with `create_claude_symlink=no`, `create_gemini_symlink=no` |
| repository | `https://github.com/telamonian/jupyter-dag` |
| advanced | no (yarn `node-modules` linker) |

Plus his instruction on the AI rules file: append the current `.claude/CLAUDE.md` to the
end of the generated `AGENTS.md`, remove `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, and replace it with a
symlink to `AGENTS.md`. No root `CLAUDE.md`.

## Steps

### 1. Generate with copier, in place

Run from the repo root. `--overwrite` is needed because `.gitignore` already exists;
`--defaults` suppresses prompts for anything not passed with `--data`.

```bash
cd ~/git/jupyter-dag
uvx --python 3.14 --from "copier~=9.2" --with jinja2-time copier copy --trust --defaults --overwrite \
  --data kind=frontend-and-server \
  --data author_name="Max Klein" \
  --data author_email=telamonian@users.noreply.github.com \
  --data labextension_name=@telamonian/jupyter-dag \
  --data python_name=jupyter_dag \
  --data project_short_description="Organize notebook cells into DAGs and run them reactively in JupyterLab" \
  --data has_settings=true --data has_binder=true --data advanced=false --data test=true \
  --data has_ai_rules=true --data create_claude_symlink=false --data create_gemini_symlink=false \
  --data repository=https://github.com/telamonian/jupyter-dag \
  https://github.com/jupyterlab/extension-template .
```

Fallback if `uvx` cannot run copier on 3.14 (jinja2-time is from 2016): install into
the venv with `uv pip install --python ~/usr/venv/jupyter-dag/bin/python "copier~=9.2" jinja2-time`
and run the same command with the venv's `copier`. Last resort: fetch the raw template
files from GitHub (paths under `template/`, Jinja braces URL-encoded) and render by hand;
the verbatim contents were captured during planning.

Afterwards confirm `.copier-answers.yml` records `_commit: v4.6.5` and the answers above,
and that no root `CLAUDE.md` or `GEMINI.md` was created.

### 2. Post-generation edits (small, all in the repo root)

- `.gitignore`: the template version replaces Max's. Re-append his three entries:
  `.history`, `*.code-workspace`, `.vscode`. (`__pycache__/`, `lib/`, `.DS_Store`, `.yarn/`
  are already covered.)
- `.prettierignore`: add `.claude` and `.history` so `jlpm prettier`/`lint` never touches
  the transcripts, settings.json, or the symlinked CLAUDE.md.
- `pyproject.toml`: add `".claude"` to `[tool.hatch.build.targets.sdist] exclude` so the
  1.3 MB transcript and design notes stay out of sdists (`.history`, `.vscode` are
  gitignored and already excluded by hatchling).
- `.github/workflows/build.yml`, `check_links` job: add `with: ignore_glob: ".claude/**"`
  to the `jupyterlab/maintainer-tools/.github/actions/check-links@v1` step so CI does not
  link-check the transcript (input name confirmed in that action's `action.yml`).
- `binder/postBuild`: replace the deprecated `jupyter labextension develop --overwrite .`
  call with `jupyter-builder develop --overwrite .` to match CONTRIBUTING.md.
- `AGENTS.md`: append a `---` separator, a short heading noting the section came from the
  former `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, then that file's content verbatim. Then
  `rm .claude/CLAUDE.md && ln -s ../AGENTS.md .claude/CLAUDE.md`. Claude Code reads
  `.claude/CLAUDE.md` through the symlink.
- Leave README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, RELEASE.md as generated (template text; wording can
  be adjusted later). Leave `version` at the template's `0.1.0`.

### 3. Install into the venv and link the extension

All commands with the venv on PATH (`export PATH=~/usr/venv/jupyter-dag/bin:$PATH`).

```bash
jlpm install          # writes yarn.lock (commit it) and .yarn/ (ignored)
jlpm build            # tsc -> lib/, then jupyter-builder build --development True . -> jupyter_dag/labextension
uv pip install --python ~/usr/venv/jupyter-dag/bin/python -e ".[dev,test]"
jupyter-builder develop --overwrite .
jupyter server extension enable jupyter_dag
```

Notes: the editable install pulls hatchling, hatch-nodejs-version, jupyter-builder,
hatch-jupyter-builder into an isolated build env and writes `jupyter_dag/_version.py`
(gitignored); its build hook skips the JS build because `labextension/static/style.js`
already exists. The `dev` extra's `jupyterlab>=4` is satisfied by the editable 4.7.0a1,
so uv must not replace it; check `uv pip list` afterwards shows jupyterlab still at
`/Users/tel/git/jupyterlab/jupyterlab`. If the bundle built against core-meta 4.6.x
fails to load in the 4.7 alpha, rebuild with
`jupyter-builder build --core-version 4.7.0-alpha.1 .` (that core-meta tag exists on npm).

### 4. Verification

- `jupyter server extension list 2>&1 | grep -i "jupyter_dag.*OK"`
- `jupyter labextension list 2>&1 | grep -i "@telamonian/jupyter-dag.*OK"`
- `pytest -vv -r ap --cov jupyter_dag` → `test_hello` passes against an authenticated server.
- `python .github/scripts/check_auth.py` → "All endpoints of the extension require authentication."
- `jlpm lint:check` and `jlpm test` (jest smoke test) pass.
- `python -m jupyterlab.browser_check` loads Lab headlessly with the extension.
- Live check: start `jupyter lab --no-browser` through the built-in browser's
  `preview_start` (add a `.claude/launch.json` entry), open `/lab`, and confirm the console
  shows `JupyterLab extension @telamonian/jupyter-dag is activated!` and the hello payload
  from `/jupyter-dag/hello`.
- `head .claude/CLAUDE.md` resolves through the symlink; `ls CLAUDE.md` fails (none at root).
- `git status`: new files are untracked and ready to commit, including `yarn.lock`,
  `ui-tests/yarn.lock` (empty), `.copier-answers.yml`; `jupyter_dag/labextension`,
  `jupyter_dag/_version.py`, `lib/`, `node_modules/`, `.yarn/` are ignored. Max commits.

## Out of scope (follow-ups, not part of this change)

- React Flow (`@xyflow/react` 12.11), react/react-dom and the matching `sharedPackages`
  block; the DAG document widget; replacing the hello route with real endpoints.
- ipykernel-side pieces (analyze_request comm target, namespace delete).
- Rewriting README/CONTRIBUTING wording to Max's style; creating the GitHub repo.
````

7	## External Documentation and Resources
8	
9	### PRIORITY RESOURCE USAGE

21	### Required External Resources
22	
23	**These resources are PRIORITY references. Always check them when you need external information:**

34	
35	3. **JupyterLab Extension Examples Repository**
36	   - URL: https://github.com/jupyterlab/extension-examples

43	   - **Action**: When implementing complex features, search this repo for how core extensions solve similar problems

46	   - URL: https://jupyter-server.readthedocs.io/
