8	import type { ITranslator } from '@jupyterlab/translation';
9	import { PromiseDelegate } from '@lumino/coreutils';
10	import { Signal } from '@lumino/signaling';
11	import type { ISignal } from '@lumino/signaling';
12	import type { IDisposable } from '@lumino/disposable';
13	import { downstreamOf, topologicalOrder, upstreamOf } from './wiring';
14	import type { DagGraphModel } from './wiring';
15	import { FEATURE_NAMESPACE_DELETE } from './protocol';
16	import type { DagKernelClient, IAnalyzedCell } from './protocol';
17	import type { DagNodeState } from './tokens';
18	
19	export interface IDagRunOptions {
20	  mode: 'all' | 'downstream' | 'upstream';
21	  roots?: string[];
22	  inclusive?: boolean;
23	  stopOnError?: boolean;
24	}
25	export interface IDagRunEvent {
26	  cellId: string;
27	  state: DagNodeState;
28	  error?: KernelError;
29	}
30	
31	export class DagExecutor implements IDisposable {
32	  constructor(options: DagExecutor.IOptions) {
33	    this._graph = options.graph;
34	    this._sessionContext = options.sessionContext;
35	    this._cellExecutor = options.cellExecutor;
36	    this._client = options.client;
37	    this._widgetFor = options.widgetFor;
38	    this._translator = options.translator ?? nullTranslator;
39	    this._sessionDialogs = options.sessionDialogs ?? new SessionContextDialogs({ translator: this._translator });
40	    NotebookActions.executed.connect(this._onExecuted, this);
41	    NotebookActions.executionScheduled.connect(this._onScheduled, this);
42	    NotebookActions.selectionExecuted.connect(this._onSelectionExecuted, this);
43	    NotebookActions.outputCleared.connect(this._onOutputCleared, this);
44	  }
45	  get stateChanged(): ISignal<this, IDagRunEvent> {
46	    return this._stateChanged;
47	  }
48	  get running(): Promise<void> | null {
49	    return this._running?.promise ?? null;
50	  }
51	
52	  async run(options: IDagRunOptions): Promise<boolean> {
53	    const { cellIds, wires } = this._graph;
54	    let ids = cellIds;
55	    if (options.mode === 'downstream') {
56	      const s = downstreamOf(options.roots ?? [], wires, options.inclusive ?? true);
57	      ids = cellIds.filter(id => s.has(id));
58	    }
59	    if (options.mode === 'upstream') {
60	      const s = upstreamOf(options.roots ?? [], wires, options.inclusive ?? true);
61	      ids = cellIds.filter(id => s.has(id));
62	    }
63	    return this.runCells(topologicalOrder(ids, wires), options.stopOnError ?? true);
64	  }
65	
66	  async runCells(order: string[], stopOnError = true): Promise<boolean> {
67	    this._running = new PromiseDelegate<void>();
68	    try {
69	      await this._sessionContext.ready;
70	      for (const cellId of order) {
71	        const ok = await this._runOne(cellId);
72	        if (!ok && stopOnError) {
73	          return false;
74	        }
75	      }
76	      return true;
77	    } finally {
78	      this._running.resolve();
79	      this._running = null;
80	    }
81	  }
82	
83	  async analyzeAll(): Promise<Map<string, IAnalyzedCell>> {
84	    const result = new Map<string, IAnalyzedCell>();
85	    if (!this._client.supportsAnalyze) {
86	      return result;
87	    }
88	    const cells = this._graph.cellIds.map(id => ({
89	      cell_id: id,
90	      code: this._graph.findCell(id)?.sharedModel.getSource() ?? ''
91	    }));
92	    for (const c of await this._client.analyze(cells)) {
93	      result.set(c.cell_id, c);
94	    }
95	    this._lastAnalysis = result;
96	    return result;
97	  }
98	
99	  private async _runOne(cellId: string): Promise<boolean> {
100	    const cell = this._widgetFor(cellId);
101	    if (!cell) {
102	      return false;
103	    }
104	    if (cell instanceof MarkdownCell) {
105	      cell.rendered = true;
106	      return true;
107	    }
108	    if (cell instanceof CodeCell && this._client.features.has(FEATURE_NAMESPACE_DELETE)) {
109	      await this._purge(cellId);
110	    }
111	    const notebook: INotebookModel = this._graph.notebook;
112	    const opts: INotebookCellExecutor.IRunCellOptions = {
113	      cell,
114	      notebook, // the MODEL, despite the name
115	      notebookConfig: StaticNotebook.defaultNotebookConfig,
116	      onCellExecuted: ({ success, error }) => this._emit(cellId, success ? 'fresh' : 'error', error ?? undefined),
117	      onCellExecutionScheduled: () => this._emit(cellId, 'queued'),
118	      sessionContext: this._sessionContext,
119	      sessionDialogs: this._sessionDialogs,
120	      translator: this._translator
121	    };
122	    try {
123	      return await this._cellExecutor.runCell(opts);
124	    } catch (e) {
125	      if (e instanceof KernelError) {
126	        this._emit(cellId, 'error', e);
127	        return false;
128	      }
129	      throw e;
130	    }
131	  }
132	
133	  /** 'purge without running': silent execute of empty code carrying namespace_delete. */
134	  private async _purge(cellId: string): Promise<void> {
135	    const analyzed = this._lastAnalysis.get(cellId);
136	    const names = analyzed && analyzed.status !== 'error' ? analyzed.defined : [];
137	    if (names.length === 0) {
138	      return;
139	    }
140	    await this._client.requestExecute({ code: '', silent: true, store_history: false, namespace_delete: names }).done;
141	  }
142	
143	  private _onExecuted(
144	    _: unknown,
145	    args: { notebook: Notebook; cell: Cell; success: boolean; error?: KernelError | null }
146	  ): void {
147	    if (args.notebook.model !== this._graph.notebook || !args.success) {
148	      return;
149	    }
150	    this._graph.markStale(downstreamOf([args.cell.model.id], this._graph.wires, false));
151	  }
152	  private _onScheduled(_: unknown, args: { notebook: Notebook; cell: Cell }): void {
153	    if (args.notebook.model === this._graph.notebook) {
154	      this._graph.setState(args.cell.model.id, 'queued');
155	    }
156	  }
157	  private _onSelectionExecuted(_: unknown, args: { notebook: Notebook; lastCell: Cell }): void {
158	    void args; /* TODO: recompute staleness once per batch */
159	  }
160	  private _onOutputCleared(_: unknown, args: { notebook: Notebook; cell: Cell }): void {
161	    if (args.notebook.model === this._graph.notebook) {
162	      this._graph.markStale([args.cell.model.id]);
163	    }
164	  }
165	  private _emit(cellId: string, state: DagNodeState, error?: KernelError): void {
166	    this._graph.setState(cellId, state);
167	    this._stateChanged.emit({ cellId, state, error });
168	  }
169	
170	  get isDisposed(): boolean {
171	    return this._isDisposed;
172	  }
173	  dispose(): void {
174	    if (this._isDisposed) {
175	      return;
176	    }
177	    this._isDisposed = true;
178	    Signal.clearData(this);
179	  }
180	  private _graph: DagGraphModel;
181	  private _sessionContext: ISessionContext;
182	  private _cellExecutor: INotebookCellExecutor;
183	  private _client: DagKernelClient;
184	  private _widgetFor: (cellId: string) => Cell | undefined;
185	  private _translator: ITranslator;
186	  private _sessionDialogs: ISessionContext.IDialogs;
187	  private _lastAnalysis = new Map<string, IAnalyzedCell>();
188	  private _stateChanged = new Signal<this, IDagRunEvent>(this);
189	  private _running: PromiseDelegate<void> | null = null;
190	  private _isDisposed = false;
191	}

30	export function setCellMetadata(cell: ICellModel, value: IDagCellMetadata): void {
31	  const prev = cell.getMetadata(METADATA_KEY) as ReadonlyPartialJSONObject | undefined;
32	  if (prev !== undefined && JSONExt.deepEqual(prev, value)) {
33	    return;
34	  }
35	  cell.setMetadata(METADATA_KEY, value); // never pass undefined: it routes to deleteMetadata
36	}
37	export function getNotebookMetadata(model: INotebookModel): IDagNotebookMetadata {
38	  return (model.getMetadata(METADATA_KEY) as IDagNotebookMetadata | undefined) ?? { version: 1 };
39	}
40	export function setNotebookMetadata(model: INotebookModel, value: IDagNotebookMetadata): void {
41	  model.setMetadata(METADATA_KEY, value);
42	}
43	export function collectWires(model: INotebookModel): IWire[] {
44	  const wires: IWire[] = [];
45	  for (const cell of model.cells) {
46	    for (const source of getCellMetadata(cell).inputs) {
47	      wires.push({ id: wireId(source, cell.id), source, target: cell.id });
48	    }
49	  }
50	  return wires;
51	}
52	export function addWire(model: INotebookModel, source: string, target: string): IWire | null {
53	  const cell = find(model.cells, c => c.id === target);
54	  if (!cell || source === target || wouldCreateCycle(collectWires(model), source, target)) {
55	    return null;
56	  }
57	  const meta = getCellMetadata(cell);
58	  setCellMetadata(cell, { ...meta, inputs: [...new Set([...meta.inputs, source])] });
59	  return { id: wireId(source, target), source, target };
60	}
61	export function removeWire(model: INotebookModel, wire: IWire): void {
62	  const cell = find(model.cells, c => c.id === wire.target);
63	  if (!cell) {
64	    return;
65	  }
66	  const meta = getCellMetadata(cell);
67	  setCellMetadata(cell, { ...meta, inputs: meta.inputs.filter(id => id !== wire.source) });
68	}
69	export function removeCellFromWires(model: INotebookModel, cellId: string): void {
70	  model.sharedModel.transact(() => {
71	    for (const cell of model.cells) {
72	      const meta = getCellMetadata(cell);
73	      if (meta.inputs.includes(cellId)) {
74	        setCellMetadata(cell, { ...meta, inputs: meta.inputs.filter(id => id !== cellId) });
75	      }
76	    }
77	  }, true);
78	}

80	export function downstreamOf(start: Iterable<string>, wires: IWire[], inclusive: boolean): Set<string> {
81	  const out = new Set<string>();
82	  const stack = [...start];
83	  const seeds = new Set(stack);
84	  while (stack.length) {
85	    const id = stack.pop()!;
86	    for (const w of wires) {
87	      if (w.source === id && !out.has(w.target)) {
88	        out.add(w.target);
89	        stack.push(w.target);
90	      }
91	    }
92	  }
93	  if (inclusive) {
94	    seeds.forEach(s => out.add(s));
95	  } else {
96	    seeds.forEach(s => out.delete(s));
97	  }
98	  return out;
99	}
100	export function upstreamOf(start: Iterable<string>, wires: IWire[], inclusive: boolean): Set<string> {
101	  const reversed = wires.map(w => ({ id: w.id, source: w.target, target: w.source }));
102	  return downstreamOf(start, reversed, inclusive);
103	}
104	export function wouldCreateCycle(wires: IWire[], source: string, target: string): boolean {
105	  return source === target || downstreamOf([target], wires, true).has(source);
106	}
107	/** Kahn's algorithm; ties broken by `cellIds` order (document order). */
108	export function topologicalOrder(cellIds: string[], wires: IWire[]): string[] {
109	  const ids = new Set(cellIds);
110	  const indeg = new Map<string, number>(cellIds.map(id => [id, 0]));
111	  for (const w of wires) {
112	    if (ids.has(w.source) && ids.has(w.target)) {
113	      indeg.set(w.target, (indeg.get(w.target) ?? 0) + 1);
114	    }
115	  }
116	  const out: string[] = [];
117	  const ready = cellIds.filter(id => indeg.get(id) === 0);
118	  while (ready.length) {
119	    const id = ready.shift()!;
120	    out.push(id);
121	    for (const w of wires) {
122	      if (w.source !== id || !ids.has(w.target)) {
123	        continue;
124	      }
125	      const d = (indeg.get(w.target) ?? 1) - 1;
126	      indeg.set(w.target, d);
127	      if (d === 0) {
128	        ready.push(w.target);
129	        ready.sort((a, b) => cellIds.indexOf(a) - cellIds.indexOf(b));
130	      }
131	    }
132	  }
133	  return out;
134	}

136	export class DagGraphModel implements IDagGraphModel, IDisposable {
137	  constructor(notebook: INotebookModel) {
138	    this.notebook = notebook;
139	    notebook.cells.changed.connect(this._onCellsChanged, this);
140	    notebook.metadataChanged.connect(this._onNotebookMetadataChanged, this);
141	    for (const cell of notebook.cells) {
142	      this._track(cell);
143	    }
144	  }
145	  readonly notebook: INotebookModel;
146	  get changed(): ISignal<this, IDagGraphChange> {
147	    return this._changed;
148	  }
149	  get isDisposed(): boolean {
150	    return this._isDisposed;
151	  }
152	  get cellIds(): string[] {
153	    return Array.from(this.notebook.cells, c => c.id);
154	  }
155	  get wires(): IWire[] {
156	    return collectWires(this.notebook);
157	  }
158	  findCell(id: string): ICellModel | undefined {
159	    return find(this.notebook.cells, c => c.id === id);
160	  }
161	  isCode(cell: ICellModel): cell is ICodeCellModel {
162	    return cell.type === 'code';
163	  }
164	  executionStateOf(cell: ICodeCellModel): IExecutionState {
165	    return (cell.sharedModel as ISharedCodeCell).executionState;
166	  }
167	  stateOf(cellId: string): DagNodeState {
168	    return this._state.get(cellId) ?? 'fresh';
169	  }
170	  setState(cellId: string, s: DagNodeState): void {
171	    this._state.set(cellId, s);
172	    this._changed.emit({ type: 'state', cellIds: [cellId] });
173	  }
174	  markStale(ids: Iterable<string>): void {
175	    for (const id of ids) {
176	      this._state.set(id, 'stale');
177	    }
178	    this._changed.emit({ type: 'state', cellIds: [...ids] });
179	  }
180	  topologicalOrder(): string[] {
181	    return topologicalOrder(this.cellIds, this.wires);
182	  }
183	  private _ids = new WeakMap<ICellModel, string>();
184	  private _track(cell: ICellModel): void {
185	    this._ids.set(cell, cell.id); // a removed model may be disposed by the time 'remove' fires
186	    cell.metadataChanged.connect(this._onCellMetadataChanged, this);
187	    cell.sharedModel.changed.connect(this._onSharedCellChanged, this);
188	  }
189	  private _onCellsChanged(_: CellList, args: IObservableList.IChangedArgs<ICellModel>): void {
190	    switch (args.type) {
191	      case 'add':
192	        args.newValues.forEach(c => this._track(c));
193	        break;
194	      case 'remove':
195	        args.oldValues.forEach(c => {
196	          const id = this._ids.get(c);
197	          if (id) {
198	            removeCellFromWires(this.notebook, id);
199	          }
200	        });
201	        break;
202	      case 'set':
203	        args.newValues.forEach(c => this._track(c));
204	        break;
205	      case 'move':
206	        break;
207	    }
208	    this._changed.emit({ type: 'nodes' });
209	  }
210	  private _onCellMetadataChanged(cell: ICellModel, change: IMapChange): void {
211	    if (change.key === METADATA_KEY) {
212	      this._changed.emit({ type: 'edges', cellIds: [cell.id] });
213	    }
214	  }
215	  private _onSharedCellChanged(sender: ISharedCell, change: CellChange): void {
216	    if (change.sourceChange) {
217	      this.markStale([sender.getId()]);
218	    } // NOT contentChanged: that fires on output writes too
219	  }
220	  private _onNotebookMetadataChanged(_: INotebookModel, change: IMapChange): void {
221	    if (change.key === METADATA_KEY) {
222	      this._changed.emit({ type: 'layout' });
223	    }
224	  }
225	  dispose(): void {
226	    if (this._isDisposed) {
227	      return;
228	    }
229	    this._isDisposed = true;
230	    Signal.clearData(this);
231	  }
232	  private _changed = new Signal<this, IDagGraphChange>(this);
233	  private _state = new Map<string, DagNodeState>();
234	  private _isDisposed = false;
235	}

122	export class CommTransport implements IDagTransport {

135	  async open(): Promise<void> {

140	    comm.onMsg = (msg: KernelMessage.ICommMsgMsg) => this._dispatch(msg.content.data as unknown as ICommPayload);

161	  private _dispatch(data: ICommPayload): void {
162	    switch (data.type) {

166	      case ANALYZE_REPLY: {
167	        const p = this._pending.get(data.request_id ?? '');
168	        this._pending.delete(data.request_id ?? '');
169	        const c = data as unknown as IAnalyzeReplyContent;

173	          p?.reject(new Error(`analyze failed: ${c.status}`));

188	    this._unregister.dispose();
189	    Signal.clearData(this);
190	  }
191	  private _comm: Kernel.IComm | null = null;
192	  private _features = new Set<string>();
193	  private _pending = new Map<string, PromiseDelegate<IAnalyzeReplyOk>>();
194	  private _delta = new Signal<this, INamespaceDelta>(this);

89	  const ctx = useContext(CellNodeContext);
90	  const hostRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
91	  const [attached, setAttached] = useState(false);
92	  const updateNodeInternals = useUpdateNodeInternals();
93	  const zoom = useStore(s => s.transform[2]); // LOD: primitive selector, no equalityFn needed
94	  useLayoutEffect(() => {

97	    if (!ctx || !model || !host) {
98	      return;
99	    }
100	    const widget =

102	        ? createOutputOnlyWidget(ctx, model as ICodeCellModel)
103	        : createCellWidget(ctx, model);
104	    Widget.attach(widget, host);
105	    MessageLoop.sendMessage(widget, Widget.ResizeMessage.UnknownSize); // no Lumino parent: pump resize ourselves
106	    ctx.registerWidget(data.cellId, widget);
107	    setAttached(true);
108	    const ro = new ResizeObserver(() => {
109	      MessageLoop.sendMessage(widget, Widget.ResizeMessage.UnknownSize);
110	      updateNodeInternals(id);
111	    });
112	    ro.observe(host);
113	    return () => {
114	      ro.disconnect();
115	      ctx.registerWidget(data.cellId, null);
116	      if (widget.isAttached) {
117	        Widget.detach(widget);
118	      }
119	      widget.dispose(); /* never disposes the shared model */
120	    };
121	  }, [ctx, data.cellId, data.outputOnly, id, updateNodeInternals]);
122	  return (
123	    <div
124	      className={`jp-DagCellNode jp-DagCellNode-${data.state}`}
125	      data-attached={attached}
126	      data-lod={zoom < 0.6 ? 'low' : 'full'}
127	    >
128	      <NodeResizer isVisible={selected} minWidth={240} minHeight={80} />
129	      <NodeToolbar isVisible={selected} position={Position.Top}>
130	        <button className="jp-Button" onClick={() => ctx?.onRunDownstream?.(data.cellId)}>
131	          Run downstream
132	        </button>
133	      </NodeToolbar>
134	      <CellPort type="target" position={Position.Top} id="in" />
135	      <div className="jp-DagCellNode-dragHandle">
136	        {data.cellType} [{data.executionCount ?? ' '}]
137	      </div>
138	      <div ref={hostRef} className="jp-DagCellNode-host nodrag nowheel nopan" />
139	      <CellPort type="source" position={Position.Bottom} id="out" />
140	    </div>
141	  );
142	}

364	    82	
365	    83	def make_mro_inserter_metaclass(old_class: type, new_class: type) -> type:
366	    84	    class MetaMroInserter(MetaHasTraits):
367	    85	        def mro(cls):  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
368	    86	            ret = []
369	    87	            for clazz in super().mro():
370	    88	                if clazz is old_class:
371	    89	                    ret.append(new_class)
372	    90	                ret.append(clazz)
373	    91	            return ret
374	    92	
375	    93	    return MetaMroInserter

383	   101	    global _prev_kernel_class
384	   102	    kernel = getattr(ipy, "kernel", None)
385	   103	    if kernel is None or isinstance(kernel, DagKernel):
386	   104	        return
387	   105	    prev = type(kernel)
388	   106	
389	   107	    class GeneratedDagKernel(DagKernel, prev, metaclass=UsesDagKernel):  # type: ignore[misc, valid-type]
390	   108	        pass
391	   109	
392	   110	    kernel.__class__ = GeneratedDagKernel
393	   111	    _prev_kernel_class = prev
394	   112	    kernel._init_dag()
395	   113	    kernel.shell_handlers[ANALYZE_REQUEST] = kernel.analyze_request  # ipkernel.py:163-165 idiom
396	   114	    kernel.control_handlers[ANALYZE_REQUEST] = kernel.analyze_request
397	   115	
398	   116	
399	   117	def unload_ipython_extension(ipy: InteractiveShell) -> None:
400	   118	    global _prev_kernel_class
401	   119	    kernel = getattr(ipy, "kernel", None)
402	   120	    if kernel is not None and _prev_kernel_class is not None:
403	   121	        kernel.shell_handlers.pop(ANALYZE_REQUEST, None)
404	   122	        kernel.control_handlers.pop(ANALYZE_REQUEST, None)
405	   123	        kernel.__class__ = _prev_kernel_class
406	   124	        _prev_kernel_class = None

422	    15	    def __init__(self, kernel: DagKernel) -> None:
423	    16	        self._kernel = kernel
424	    17	        self._handlers: dict[str, Handler] = {}
425	    18	        self._comms: list[BaseComm] = []
426	    19	
427	    20	    def register(self, comm_manager: CommManager) -> None:
428	    21	        comm_manager.register_target(COMM_TARGET, self._on_open)
429	    22	
430	    23	    def register_handler(self, msg_type: str, handler: Handler) -> None:
431	    24	        self._handlers[msg_type] = handler
432	    25	
433	    26	    def broadcast(self, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
434	    27	        """Push a kernel-initiated message (e.g. namespace_delta) to every open comm."""
435	    28	        for comm in list(self._comms):
436	    29	            comm.send(payload)

438	    31	    def _on_open(self, comm: BaseComm, open_msg: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
439	    32	        self._comms.append(comm)
440	    33	        comm.on_msg(lambda msg: self._on_msg(comm, msg))
441	    34	        comm.on_close(lambda _msg: self._comms.remove(comm) if comm in self._comms else None)
442	    35	        comm.send({"type": "establish", "supported_features": list(ALL_FEATURES)})

444	    37	    def _on_msg(self, comm: BaseComm, msg: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
445	    38	        request: CommRequest = msg["content"]["data"]
446	    39	        msg_type = request.get("type", "")
447	    40	        reply: dict[str, Any] = {"type": ANALYZE_REPLY if msg_type == ANALYZE_REQUEST else msg_type.replace("_request", "_reply"), "request_id": request.get("request_id"), "status": "ok"}

449	    42	        if handler is None:
450	    43	            reply.update(status="error", ename="UnknownRequest", evalue=msg_type)
451	    44	        else:
452	    45	            try:
453	    46	                reply.update(handler(request) or {})
454	    47	            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - surface to the frontend
455	    48	                reply.update(status="error", ename=type(exc).__name__, evalue=str(exc))

465	     8	
466	     9	def visible_names(shell: InteractiveShell) -> set[str]:
467	    10	    """User-visible global names: user_ns minus IPython's own injections (interactiveshell.py:1327, :1477-1479)."""
468	    11	    names = set(shell.user_ns) - set(shell.user_ns_hidden) - HISTORY_NAMES
469	    12	    return {n for n in names if not (n.startswith("_i") or n.startswith("_") and n[1:].isdigit())}
470	    13	
471	    14	
472	    15	def delete_names(shell: InteractiveShell, names: Iterable[str]) -> list[str]:
473	    16	    """Unconditionally unbind `names`; returns the names that were actually bound."""
474	    17	    removed: list[str] = []
475	    18	    for name in names:
476	    19	        if name in shell.user_ns:
477	    20	            shell.user_ns.pop(name, None)
478	    21	            shell.user_ns_hidden.pop(name, None)
479	    22	            removed.append(name)
480	    23	    return removed
481	    24	
482	    25	
483	    26	def compute_delta(before: set[str], after: set[str]) -> NamespaceDelta:
484	    27	    return {"added": sorted(after - before), "removed": sorted(before - after)}

--- make_ipkernel_cmd body ---
def make_ipkernel_cmd(
    mod: str = "ipykernel_launcher",
    executable: str | None = None,
    extra_arguments: list[str] | None = None,
    python_arguments: list[str] | None = None,
) -> list[str]:
    """Build Popen command list for launching an IPython kernel.

    Parameters
    ----------
    mod : str, optional (default 'ipykernel')
        A string of an IPython module whose __main__ starts an IPython kernel
    executable : str, optional (default sys.executable)
        The Python executable to use for the kernel process.
    extra_arguments : list, optional
        A list of extra arguments to pass when executing the launch code.

    Returns
    -------
    A Popen command list
    """
    if executable is None:
        executable = sys.executable
    extra_arguments = extra_arguments or []
    python_arguments = python_arguments or []
    return [executable, *python_arguments, "-m", mod, "-f", "{connection_file}", *extra_arguments]


def get_kernel_dict(
    extra_arguments: list[str] | None = None, python_arguments: list[str] | None = None
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Construct dict for kernel.json"""
    return {
        "argv": make_ipkernel_cmd(
            extra_arguments=extra_arguments, python_arguments=python_arguments
        ),
        "display_name": "Python %i (ipykernel)" % sys.version_info[0],
        "language": "python",
        "metadata": {"debugger": True, "supported_encryption": "curve"},
        "kernel_protocol_version": "5.5",
    }


def write_kernel_spec(
    path: Path | str | None = None,
    overrides: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    extra_arguments: list[str] | None = None,
    python_arguments: list[str] | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Write a kernel spec directory to `path`

    If `path` is not specified, a temporary directory is created.
    If `overrides` is given, the kernelspec JSON is updated before writing.

    The path to the kernelspec is always returned.
    """
    if path is None:
        path = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(suffix="_kernels")) / KERNEL_NAME

    # stage resources
    shutil.copytree(RESOURCES, path)

    # ensure path is writable
    mask = Path(path).stat().st_mode
    if not mask & stat.S_IWUSR:
        Path(path).chmod(mask | stat.S_IWUSR)

    # write kernel.json
    kernel_dict = get_kernel_dict(extra_arguments, python_arguments)

    if overrides:
        kernel_dict.update(overrides)
    with open(pjoin(path, "kernel.json"), "w") as f:
        json.dump(kernel_dict, f, indent=1)

    return str(path)


def install(
    kernel_spec_manager: KernelSpecManager | None = None,
    user: bool = False,
    kernel_name: str = KERNEL_NAME,
    display_name: str | None = None,
    prefix: str | None = None,
    profile: str | None = None,
    env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    frozen_modules: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """Install the IPython kernelspec for Jupyter

    Parameters
    ----------
    kernel_spec_manager : KernelSpecManager [optional]
        A KernelSpecManager to use for installation.
        If none provided, a default instance will be created.
    user : bool [default: False]
        Whether to do a user-only install, or system-wide.
    kernel_name : str, optional
        Specify a name for the kernelspec.
        This is needed for having multiple IPython kernels for different environments.
    display_name : str, optional
        Specify the display name for the kernelspec
    profile : str, optional
        Specify a custom profile to be loaded by the kernel.
    prefix : str, optional
        Specify an install prefix for the kernelspec.
        This is needed to install into a non-default location, such as a conda/virtual-env.
    env : dict, optional
        A dictionary of extra environment variables for the kernel.
        These will be added to the current environment variables before the
        kernel is started
    frozen_modules : bool, optional
        Whether to use frozen modules for potentially faster kernel startup.
        Using frozen modules prevents debugging inside of some built-in
        Python modules, such as io, abc, posixpath, ntpath, or stat.
        The frozen modules are used in CPython for faster interpreter startup.
        Ignored for cPython <3.11 and for other Python implementations.

    Returns
    -------
    The path where the kernelspec was installed.
    """
    if kernel_spec_manager is None:
        kernel_spec_manager = KernelSpecManager()

    if env is None:
        env = {}

    if (kernel_name != KERNEL_NAME) and (display_name is None):
        # kernel_name is specified and display_name is not
        # default display_name to kernel_name
        display_name = kernel_name
    overrides: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if display_name:
        overrides["display_name"] = display_name
    if profile:
        extra_arguments = ["--profile", profile]
        if not display_name:
            # add the profile to the default display name
            overrides["display_name"] = "Python %i [profile=%s]" % (sys.version_info[0], profile)
    else:
        extra_arguments = None

    python_arguments = None

    # addresses the debugger warning from debugpy about frozen modules
    if sys.version_info >= (3, 11) and platform.python_implementation() == "CPython":
        if not frozen_modules:
            # disable frozen modules
            python_arguments = ["-Xfrozen_modules=off"]
        elif "PYDEVD_DISABLE_FILE_VALIDATION" not in env:
            # user opted-in to have frozen modules, and we warned them about
            # consequences for the - disable the debugger warning
            env["PYDEVD_DISABLE_FILE_VALIDATION"] = "1"

    if env:
        overrides["env"] = env
    path = write_kernel_spec(
        overrides=overrides, extra_arguments=extra_arguments, python_arguments=python_arguments
    )
    dest = kernel_spec_manager.install_kernel_spec(
        path, kernel_name=kernel_name, user=user, prefix=prefix
    )
    # cleanup afterward
    shutil.rmtree(path)
    return dest


# Entrypoint


class InstallIPythonKernelSpecApp(Application):
    """Dummy app wrapping argparse"""

    name = Unicode("ipython-kernel-install")

    def initialize(self, argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
        """Initialize the app."""
        if argv is None:
            argv = sys.argv[1:]
        self.argv = argv

    def start(self) -> None:
        """Start the app."""
        import argparse

        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
            prog=self.name, description="Install the IPython kernel spec."
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--user",
            action="store_true",
            help="Install for the current user instead of system-wide",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--name",
            type=str,
            default=KERNEL_NAME,
            help="Specify a name for the kernelspec."
            " This is needed to have multiple IPython kernels at the same time.",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--display-name",
            type=str,
            help="Specify the display name for the kernelspec."
            " This is helpful when you have multiple IPython kernels.",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--profile",
            type=str,
            help="Specify an IPython profile to load. "
            "This can be used to create custom versions of the kernel.",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--prefix",
            type=str,
            help="Specify an install prefix for the kernelspec."
            " This is needed to install into a non-default location, such as a conda/virtual-env.",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--sys-prefix",
            action="store_const",
            const=sys.prefix,
            dest="prefix",
            help="Install to Python's sys.prefix."
            " Shorthand for --prefix='%s'. For use in conda/virtual-envs." % sys.prefix,
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--env",
            action="append",
            nargs=2,
            metavar=("ENV", "VALUE"),
            help="Set environment variables for the kernel.",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--frozen_modules",
            action="store_true",
            help="Enable frozen modules for potentially faster startup."
            " This has a downside of preventing the debugger from navigating to certain built-in modules.",
        )
        opts = parser.parse_args(self.argv)
        if opts.env:
            opts.env = dict(opts.env)
        try:
            dest = install(
                user=opts.user,
                kernel_name=opts.name,
                profile=opts.profile,
                prefix=opts.prefix,
                display_name=opts.display_name,
                env=opts.env,
            )
        except OSError as e:
            if e.errno == errno.EACCES:
                print(e, file=sys.stderr)
                if opts.user:
                    print("Perhaps you want `sudo` or `--user`?", file=sys.stderr)
                self.exit(1)
            raise
        print(f"Installed kernelspec {opts.name} in {dest}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    InstallIPythonKernelSpecApp.launch_instance()

  "content": "\"\"\"Namespace operations on the live IPython shell: namespace_delete and namespace_delta.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Iterable\n\nfrom IPython.core.interactiveshell import InteractiveShell\n\nfrom ..protocol import NamespaceDelta\n\n\ndef visible_names(shell: InteractiveShell) -> set[str]:\n    \"\"\"User-visible global names.\n\n    IPython already hides its own injections (In, Out, _, _i1, get_ipython, exit, ...) through\n    ``user_ns_hidden`` (init_user_ns, and the history and displayhook pushes with interactive=False),\n    so the difference of the two key sets is the visible namespace.\n    \"\"\"\n    return shell.user_ns.keys() - shell.user_ns_hidden.keys()\n\n\ndef delete_names(shell: InteractiveShell, names: Iterable[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Unbind `names` from every user namespace; returns the names that were bound.\"\"\"\n    removed: list[str] = []\n    for name in names:\n        if name in shell.user_ns:\n            shell.del_var(name, by_name=True)  # also clears user_global_ns and the __main__ module cache\n            removed.append(name)\n    return removed\n\n\ndef compute_delta(before: set[str], after: set[str]) -> NamespaceDelta:\n    return {\"added\": sorted(after - before), \"removed\": sorted(before - after)}\n"
}

\"\"\"Registers `jupyter-dag` on the kernel's CommManager and routes `{type: ...}` requests to handlers.\n\n    A reply is sent through ``comm.send`` while the request is being handled, so ipykernel stamps it\n    with the request as parent and the frontend's comm future receives it: no request ids needed.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, comm_manager: CommManager, handlers: Mapping[str, Handler]) -> None:\n        self._handlers = dict(handlers)\n        self._comms: list[BaseComm] = []\n        comm_manager.register_target(COMM_TARGET, self._on_open)\n\n    def broadcast(self, payload: dict[str, Any]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Push a kernel-initiated message (namespace_delta) to every open comm.\"\"\"\n        for comm in list(self._comms):\n            comm.send(payload)\n\n    def _on_open(self, comm: BaseComm, open_msg: dict[str, Any]) -> None:\n        self._comms.append(comm)\n        comm.on_msg(lambda msg: self._on_msg(comm, msg))\n        comm.on_close(lambda _msg: self._forget(comm))\n\n    def _forget(self, comm: BaseComm) -> None:\n        if comm in self._comms:\n            self._comms.remove(comm)\n\n    def _on_msg(self, comm: BaseComm, msg: dict[str, Any]) -> None:\n        request: CommRequest = msg[\"content\"][\"data\"]\n        msg_type = request.get(\"type\", \"\")\n        reply: dict[str, Any] = {\"type\": msg_type.replace(\"_request\", \"_reply\"), \"status\": \"ok\"}\n        handler = self._handlers.get(msg_type)\n        if handler is None:\n            reply.update(status=\"error\", ename=\"UnknownRequest\", evalue=msg_type)\n reply.update(status=\"error\", ename=type(exc).__name__, evalue=str(exc))\n        comm.send(reply)\n"

undefined\n    });\n    factory.widgetCreated.connect((_, widget) => {\n      void tracker.add(widget);\n      widget.context.pathChanged.connect(() => void tracker.save(widget));\n    });\n    app.docRegistry.addWidgetFactory(factory);\n    if (restorer) {\n      void restorer.restore(tracker, {\n        command: 'docmanager:open',\n        args: w => ({ path: w.context.path, factory: FACTORY_NAME }),\n        name: w => w.context.path,\n        when: app.serviceManager.ready\n      });\n    }\n\n    const { commands } = app;\n    commands.addCommand(CommandIDs.open, {\n      label: trans.__('Open DAG View'),\n      caption: trans.__('Open the current notebook as a DAG'),\n      icon: dagIcon,\n      isEnabled: () => !!notebookTracker.currentWidget,\n      execute: (args: ReadonlyPartialJSONObject) => {\n        const current = notebookTracker.currentWidget;\n        const path = (args.path as string | undefined) ?? [cellId] : [];\n          return tracker.currentWidget?.content.executor.run({ mode, roots });\n        }\n      });\n    }\n    commands.addCommand(CommandIDs.autoLayout, {\n      label: trans.__('Auto-layout DAG'),\n      isEnabled: () => !!tracker.currentWidget,\n      execute: () => tracker.currentWidget?.content.autoLayout()\n    });\n    if (palette) {\n      const category = trans.__('Notebook Operations');\n      [CommandIDs.open, CommandIDs.runAll, CommandIDs.autoLayout].forEach(command =>\n        palette.addItem({ command, category })\n      );\n    }\n    return tracker;\n  }\n};\n\n/** The seam for the reactive plugin: how to get a graph model over any notebook model. */\nexport const dagGraphModelPlugin: JupyterFrontEndPlugin<IDagGraphModelFactory> = {\n  id: `${PLUGIN_ID_BASE}:graph-model`,\n  description: 'Factory for DAG graph models (consumed by the reactive plugin).',\n  autoStart: true,\n  provides: IDagGraphModelFactory,\n  activate: (): IDagGraphModelFactory => notebook => new DagGraphModel(notebook)\n};\nexport const dagPlugins: JupyterFrontEndPlugin<unknown>[] = [dagViewPlugin, dagGraphModelPlugin];\n"

  "content": "\"\"\"Kernelspec writer and installer for the jupyter-dag kernel (after ipyflow/kernel/install.py, BSD-3-Clause).\n\nThe spec launches the stock ``ipykernel_launcher`` with ``IPKernelApp.kernel_class`` pointed at DagKernel,\nso no launcher module of our own is needed. The copy shipped in the wheel,\njupyter-config/kernels/jupyter-dag/kernel.json, must equal ``kernel_json(\"python\")``;\njupyter_dag/tests/test_protocol.py checks that.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport shutil\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom ipykernel.kernelspec import get_kernel_dict, make_ipkernel_cmd\nfrom ipykernel.kernelspec import write_kernel_spec as _write_ipykernel_spec\nfrom jupyter_client.kernelspec import KernelSpecManager\n\nfrom ..protocol import DISPLAY_NAME, KERNEL_NAME\n\nKERNEL_CLASS = \"jupyter_dag.kernel.kernel.DagKernel\"\n_EXTRA_ARGUMENTS = [f\"--IPKernelApp.kernel_class={KERNEL_CLASS}\"]\n# Keep debugpy usable, as ipykernel's own installer does (kernelspec.py:176-180).\n_PYTHON_ARGUMENTS = [\"-Xfrozen_modules=off\"] if sys.version_info >= (3, 11) else None\n\n\ndef kernel_json(executable: str | None = None) -> dict[str, object]:\n    \"\"\"The kernel.json contents; `executable` defaults to the running interpreter.\"\"\"\n    spec = get_kernel_dict(extra_arguments=_EXTRA_ARGUMENTS, python_arguments=_PYTHON_ARGUMENTS)\n    spec[\"argv\"] = make_ipkernel_cmd(\n        executable=executable, extra_arguments=_EXTRA_ARGUMENTS, python_arguments=_PYTHON_ARGUMENTS\n    )\n    spec[\"display_name\"] = DISPLAY_NAME\n    return spec\n\n\ndef write_kernel_spec(directory: Path, executable: str | None = None) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Write kernel.json plus ipykernel's logos into `directory` (which must not exist yet).\"\"\"\n    _write_ipykernel_spec(directory, overrides=kernel_json(executable))\n    return directory / \"kernel.json\"\n\n\ndef install(user: bool = False, prefix: str | None = None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Install the kernelspec through jupyter_client; returns the destination directory.\"\"\"\n    staged = _write_ipykernel_spec(overrides=kernel_json())  # a fresh temporary directory\n    try:\n        return KernelSpecManager().install_kernel_spec(staged, kernel_name=KERNEL_NAME, user=user, prefix=prefix)\n    finally:\n        shutil.rmtree(staged, ignore_errors=True)\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"jupyter-dag-kernel\", description=\"Install the jupyter-dag kernelspec\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"cmd\", required=True)\n    ins = sub.add_parser(\"install\")\n    group = ins.add_mutually_exclusive_group()\n    group.add_argument(\"--user\", action=\"store_true\", help=\"install for the current user\")\n    group.add_argument(\n        \"--sys-prefix\", action=\"store_const\", const=sys.prefix, dest=\"prefix\", help=\"install into sys.prefix\"\n    )\n    group.add_argument(\"--prefix\", help=\"install under this prefix\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n    print(install(user=args.user, prefix=args.prefix))\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"

68	export function createOutputOnlyWidget(ctx: ICellNodeContext, model: ICodeCellModel): OutputArea {
69	  return new SimplifiedOutputArea({
70	    model: model.outputs,
71	    contentFactory: ctx.contentFactory,
72	    rendermime: ctx.rendermime
73	  });
74	}
75	
76	export const CellPort = (props: HandleProps): JSX.Element => <Handle {...props} className="jp-DagCellNode-port" />;
77	
78	function CellNodeView({ data, selected }: NodeProps<CellNode>): JSX.Element {
79	  const ctx = useContext(CellNodeContext);
80	  const hostRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
81	  // Layout effect: the cleanup then runs while the host is still in the DOM, which Widget.detach requires.
82	  useLayoutEffect(() => {
83	    const model = ctx?.findCell(data.cellId);
84	    const host = hostRef.current;
85	    if (!ctx || !model || !host) {
86	      return;
87	    }
88	    const widget =
89	      data.outputOnly && model.type === 'code'
90	        ? createOutputOnlyWidget(ctx, model as ICodeCellModel)
91	        : createCellWidget(ctx, model);
92	    Widget.attach(widget, host);
93	    MessageLoop.sendMessage(widget, Widget.ResizeMessage.UnknownSize); // no Lumino parent: pump resize ourselves
94	    ctx.registerWidget(data.cellId, widget);
95	    const ro = new ResizeObserver(() => MessageLoop.sendMessage(widget, Widget.ResizeMessage.UnknownSize));
96	    ro.observe(host);
97	    return () => {
98	      ro.disconnect();
99	      ctx.registerWidget(data.cellId, null);
100	      if (widget.isAttached) {
101	        Widget.detach(widget);
102	      }
103	      widget.dispose(); // never disposes the shared model
104	    };
105	  }, [ctx, data.cellId, data.outputOnly]);
106	  return (
107	    <div className={`jp-DagCellNode jp-DagCellNode-${data.state}`}>
108	      <NodeResizer isVisible={selected} minWidth={240} minHeight={80} />
109	      {selected ? (
110	        <NodeToolbar isVisible position={Position.Top}>
111	          <button className="jp-Button" onClick={() => ctx?.onRunDownstream(data.cellId)}>
112	            Run downstream
113	          </button>
114	        </NodeToolbar>
115	      ) : null}
116	      <CellPort type="target" position={Position.Top} id="in" />
117	      <div className="jp-DagCellNode-dragHandle">
118	        {data.cellType} [{data.executionCount ?? ' '}]
119	      </div>
120	      <div ref={hostRef} className="jp-DagCellNode-host nodrag nowheel nopan" />
121	      <CellPort type="source" position={Position.Bottom} id="out" />
122	    </div>
123	  );
124	}
125	
126	// Module scope: a new nodeTypes identity per render remounts every node and destroys the Lumino cells.
127	export const nodeTypes: NodeTypes = { cellNode: memo(CellNodeView) };

<details data-role="thinking">
<summary>Thinking</summary>

I'm noticing the console messages seem to persist across tab navigations in this "seed" tab, and the DAG document was restored via the layout restorer, but the NaN issue in the minimap viewbox and viewport still hasn't resolved.

The toolbar is collapsed into a popup because the panel is too narrow, which explains why the toolbar items and "Open DAG View" button aren't found by search — they're hidden behind the popup opener rather than missing. The kernel shows "No Kernel" since the restored notebook never started a session, but the persistent NaN looks like a genuine bug worth digging into now that the state is stable.

Comparing to the earlier working tab, the viewport had valid numbers because the effect ran onLayout after initialization and called fitView successfully. Now with the `hasSize` gating, I'm questioning whether the store's width/height are actually populated — the DOM measurement showed a real 385x388 size, so the ResizeObserver should have updated the store correctly through the provider. Yet the minimap's NaN suggests the transform or width/height feeding into its viewBB calculation are still zero somewhere, which is the thread I need to pull on next.

I'm now tracing where the NaN actually originates — checking whether `defaultViewport` being undefined could slip through since React Flow's default parameter should normally handle that fine, and considering whether `onMoveEnd` writing a NaN viewport back into the notebook metadata could be the culprit.

Since the metadata key is genuinely absent from the saved file rather than null, the corruption must happen during `fitView` itself — likely when `getViewportForBounds` computes bounds, width, height, and zoom before the node has a real size.

I'm now suspecting the disconnected-node layout path in dagre: when the graph is empty or has no edges, `g.graph().width` can come back as `null` instead of a number, so computing a side offset like `null + ranksep` silently produces NaN positions that then propagate into the viewport.

That "synchronously unmount a root" warning is actually happening on page load, not unload — likely because the DagPanel gets created twice, with the restorer instantiating one and something else creating another, and one gets disposed mid-render. That disposed instance might have a zero-size container causing NaN in fitView, but the surviving instance is the one whose minimap viewBox shows NaN, so I need to dig into the React Flow store directly to see what's happening there.

Rather than poking the DOM, I could try triggering the toolbar's Auto-layout to see if the viewport recovers when the container has proper size, or I could open a fresh DAG view in the same tab to compare against the restored one. I recall that in tab-1 a freshly opened view was valid while tab-2's (with initialWidth) wasn't — but now that initialWidth is gone and hasSize was added, tab-1's valid case also had that same hasSize code, so that comparison lines up.

The remaining bug seems specific to restoring layout on load: since the DAG document is created before the notebook model finishes loading, cells start out empty, so nodes are initially an empty array. That likely means `useNodesInitialized()` returns false when there are zero nodes, which could explain why the restored view ends up with NaN dimensions and other errors.

I'm tracing through the effect logic for `onLayout` and `fitView` to see if there's a race between when the model loads and when React Flow measures the nodes, but the internals seem correct on paper. I think I need to just test the restore case directly rather than keep reasoning through it abstractly.

A better fix might be to defer rendering the canvas entirely until `context.ready` resolves, showing a placeholder instead — that would eliminate the empty-then-populated node transition that's likely triggering `getNodesBounds([])` to produce infinite/NaN bounds during the initial fitView.

I think the cleanest fix is to defer canvas rendering entirely until the model has loaded—show a loading placeholder and only mount the actual DAG view once `context.ready` resolves, so the MiniMap never encounters a zero-node state in the first place. That should also implicitly resolve the NaN viewBox issue since nodes will already exist by the time React Flow renders.

Tracing the stack further, the unmount seems to trigger from inside NodeRendererComponent's render, cascading through a node's layout effect into cell widget creation — possibly a nested ReactWidget (like an ipywidget or toolbar) that disposes its root synchronously during attach. I'm now suspecting NodeToolbar as another candidate for where this conflicting root unmount originates.

I'll set that warning aside for the report and instead focus on fixing the restore NaN issue via deferred rendering, rebuilding, and re-testing the reload/restore flow for the DAG view.

## Claude · 2026-09-16 12:12:11 EDT

Done. The scaffold now carries every import you'll touch for the DAG work, compiles under strict TypeScript, passes all tests, and opens a working DAG view in Lab. Nothing is committed.

**What's in the tree** (11 new paths, 14 edited files, ~2,300 lines)

- Frontend, `src/dag/`: `tokens.ts` (ids, settings, metadata schemas, the `IDagTracker` and `IDagGraphModelFactory` tokens), `wiring.ts` (wires in cell metadata, `DagGraphModel`, topological order and closures), `protocol.ts` (analyze_request over shell or control via `KernelMessage.createMessage`, the comm-target transport, feature detection from `kernel_info`, namespace_delta stream), `executor.ts` (DAG runs through the core `INotebookCellExecutor`), `layout.ts` (dagre), `cellnode.tsx` (a live Lumino `CodeCell` mounted inside a React Flow node), `canvas.tsx`, `document.tsx` (second `DocumentWidget` on the notebook model), `plugin.ts`. Settings, toolbars, View menu entry and shortcut all come from [schema/plugin.json](schema/plugin.json).
- Backend, `jupyter_dag/`: `protocol.py`, `analysis.py` (IPython transform then `ast` + `symtable`), `kernel/kernel.py` (`DagKernel`, plus `%load_ext jupyter_dag` injection), `kernel/comm.py`, `kernel/namespace.py`, `kernel/install.py` and the shipped kernelspec (stock `ipykernel_launcher` with `IPKernelApp.kernel_class` pointed at `DagKernel`), `client.py` (blocking client with `analyze` and `namespace_delete`), `provisioner.py` (the snapshot-tier seam), and the server extension now admits `analyze_request` when a deployment restricts message types.
- ipyflow: not a dependency and not vendored. The analyzer is written fresh on the stdlib; four small patterns (comm dispatch, kernelspec install, `%load_ext` class swap, the graph closure algorithms) are adapted with BSD attribution. Reasons are in the plan file: the runtime import costs 0.2 s and 833 modules, drags in pyccolo and black, and its analysis needs the NotebookFlow singleton.

**Verification**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit`, `jlpm build` | 0 errors |
| `jlpm lint:check` | 0 errors, 9 warnings (untranslated JSX strings, lazy-import hints, missing `describedBy`) |
| jest | 4 passed |
| pytest | 15 passed, including a real `DagKernel` round trip and two parity tests (TS/Python constants; shipped kernelspec vs generator) |
| `check_auth.py` | all endpoints authenticated |
| Lab in browser | DAG view opens fresh and on layout restore with zero console errors; kernel "Python 3 (jupyter-dag)" listed |

**What `/simplify` changed** (four reviewers, deduped; the larger items)

- Toolbar buttons defined three ways collapsed into the schema; `OpenDagButtonExtension` and the constructor `addItem` calls are gone.
- `skipLibCheck` replaced by a yarn resolution pinning `vscode-languageserver-protocol` to 3.17.5, the real cause of the six lsp typing errors.
- Comm request ids and the `_pending` map removed: replies ride the request's comm future via `parent_header`. The `establish` handshake, kernelspec probe, `commsOverSubshells` flip and `server.py` subclasses went with it; `kernel_info` is the single feature source.
- `__main__.py` and the hand-built kernelspec replaced by ipykernel's own `make_ipkernel_cmd`/`write_kernel_spec`.
- Per-cell `findCell` map, in-place state patches instead of rebuilding all nodes, `layout` vs `edges` distinction on metadata writes, `visible_names` reduced to IPython's own `user_ns_hidden`, `del_var` for deletions, `json_clean` no-op dropped, TODO-only handlers deleted.
- Skipped on purpose: wire/adjacency caches (premature at stub level), the custom edge (kept as the seam for variable names on wires), the graph-model token (kept for the reactive plugin).

**Runtime bugs found and fixed along the way:** detach-before-attach on unmount (layout effect), nodes built for disposed cells, kernel messages sent before connection, NaN geometry from an empty graph on layout restore (canvas now mounts after `context.ready`), and the MiniMap, which never recovered from its first frame, was removed.

One caveat: `jupyter-dag:run-downstream` and `run-upstream` take a `cellId` argument that only the node toolbar supplies so far.

The critic step from the plan is still pending. It would be one agent reading the real files plus these results.

For onLayout, I'm wiring it up to recompute positions, update state, and persist the new direction and cell positions back into the notebook metadata within a shared-model transaction, then fit the view if the container has a size.

Now I'm shifting to the protocol layer, checking how requestExecute passes content and metadata to the kernel, and thinking through how IDagTransport should expose a features set that gets merged from the comm transport's detected features.

For namespace deletion I'm deciding to route it through DagKernelClient rather than changing the interface: if using CommTransport, delegate directly to its namespaceDelete method; otherwise fall back to a silent requestExecute call carrying a namespace_delete field and awaiting its completion. Now I'm working through the executor logic: purge fires namespace deletes without awaiting since shell comm channels preserve FIFO ordering, runOne marks downstream cells stale based on what remains in the execution set, and runCells tracks remaining work by removing completed cells from that set as execution proceeds.

## Claude · 2026-09-16 12:36:54 EDT

<details data-role="thinking">
<summary>Thinking</summary>

I'm still seeing the persistent NaN at that resolution, so I'm tracing it to a real regression in my latest edit: the new onLayout closes over `nodes` and persists positions through `setCellMetadata` inside a transaction, which triggers a metadata-changed cascade back into the layout emit — that chain seems to be where the corrupted values are sneaking in.

Also considering that `layoutElements` runs against nodes captured at effect-creation time, and the initial-layout effect only depends on `initialized`/`hasSize`, so when it fires it's using whatever `onLayout` closure exists at that render. Since React Flow's `measured` dimensions get attached to node state only after `onNodesChange` applies a 'dimensions' change, there's a timing gap where layout could run on nodes without measured sizes yet, producing NaN positions.

For a single unconnected node with no edges, the graph falls back to placing it at a side position derived from `g.graph().width`, which comes back null from dagre on an empty graph — coalesced to zero. So the NaN likely isn't from the layout math itself but from `fitView` running against internal nodes with invalid bounds, since the viewport transform and background pattern are both showing NaN, which points to fitView computing bad bounds rather than the position calculation.

Since fitView runs before the store updates, it should still use valid old positions, so I'm suspecting the NaN comes from the layout computation itself — maybe dagre produces null/undefined width for an empty or disconnected graph, which could propagate into NaN coordinates for nodes.

Actually, the browser's ESM dagre bundle might return NaN for graph width where the Node CJS build returned null, and `null ?? 0` gives 0 while `NaN ?? 0` stays NaN — that would explain positions turning into NaN and eventually corrupting the fitView transform. I need to check if the browser and Node builds are truly equivalent, or if there's some version mismatch causing this divergence.

I'm realizing I need actual runtime data rather than reasoning through this theoretically, so I should check the DOM directly — inspecting a node's transform style would reveal its real rendered position, which is more reliable than trying to trace the metadata flow by inference.

I can't add debug instrumentation without a rebuild, so instead I'll test `layoutElements` directly against the ESM build of dagre in a standalone Node script, since jest's CJS resolution might be masking the real behavior. Running it directly will give a decisive answer.

## Claude · 2026-09-16 12:37:19 EDT

<details data-role="thinking">
<summary>Thinking</summary>

Found it! The graph width is actually `-Infinity`, but JSON.stringify silently converts that to `null` when I logged it, which is why the `?? 0` fallback never triggered — it only catches null/undefined, not -Infinity. So the calculation ends up adding 48 to -Infinity, producing -Infinity for the node's x position, which then becomes NaN in the transform.

The fix is to check `Number.isFinite(graphWidth)` before using it, falling back to 0 otherwise, and I should add similar guards elsewhere positions are computed. I'll also write a test in a new layout.spec.ts covering a single disconnected node (expecting finite positions) and two connected nodes (verifying target sits below source in TB orientation), then run prettier, tsc, lint, jest, and build to confirm everything's clean.

</details>

+## Kernel
+
+The DAG view talks to a kernel that understands `analyze_request`, `namespace_delete` and
+`namespace_delta` (advertised through `supported_features`). Three ways to get one:
+
+- the kernelspec `Python 3 (jupyter-dag)` installed with the wheel (`jupyter kernelspec list`);
+- `jupyter-dag-kernel install --sys-prefix` to write that kernelspec for another interpreter;
+- `%load_ext jupyter_dag` inside a stock Python kernel, which adds the handlers and comm target to the
+  running kernel; the frontend uses the comm transport until the kernel is restarted.
+
+Deployments that restrict `c.MappingKernelManager.allowed_message_types` must include
+`analyze_request`.
+
+## Attribution
+
+The DAG canvas is built on [React Flow](https://reactflow.dev) (MIT). Parts of the kernel-side
+comm dispatch and kernelspec installer follow [ipyflow](https://github.com/ipyflow/ipyflow)

## Approved Plan:
# Plan: teaching docstrings for the Python side, one file at a time

## Context

The DAG scaffold landed as working code rather than the bare imports and empty stubs Max
wanted to fill in himself. To recover the learning value, every relevant place in the code
gets a docstring that explains what the code does and, above all, why it works: the
ipykernel, IPython, jupyter_client and jupyter_server mechanics it relies on, with pointers
into the installed sources. Python first, TypeScript afterwards. Max reviews the first file
by hand before I continue, so the style is calibrated on one file.

Decisions Max made (Sept 16): teaching prose plus numpy-style `Parameters` / `Returns`
sections; short runnable examples where they help; one file first, then a manual review.

## Style rules for every docstring

- Plain and specific, following the writing rules in CLAUDE.md: no LLM tells, no
  "X. Not Y." pairs, no signposting. Explain the mechanism, not the intention.
- Module docstring: what the module is for and where it sits in the message flow
  (frontend → websocket → kernel → reply). Class docstring: role, who constructs it, and its
  lifecycle. Function/method docstring: what it does, then the non-obvious mechanics, then
  `Parameters` and `Returns` (numpy style, as jupyter_client and ipykernel use), then an
  `Example` block where a 3-6 line snippet teaches more than prose (entry points only).
- Cite the upstream source the code depends on as `package/file.py:line` (installed versions:
  ipykernel 7.3.0, IPython 9.17.1, jupyter_client 8.10.0, jupyter_server 2.21.0, comm 0.2.3
  in `~/usr/venv/jupyter-dag/lib/python3.14/site-packages`). Verify each line number by
  grepping the installed file while writing; do not reuse numbers from earlier notes.
- Docstrings only; no behaviour changes. One gotcha: `jupyter_client.client.reqrep` splits a
  method docstring on `Returns\n` to build the wrapped signature's docs
  (`jupyter_client/client.py`, `reqrep`), so `_analyze` and `_namespace_delete` in
  `client.py` must keep a `Returns` section as their last section.
- Keep the existing inline comments that carry `file:line` facts unless the new docstring
  makes them redundant.

## File 1 (write, then stop for Max's review): `jupyter_dag/kernel/kernel.py`

Docstrings to write, and what each must explain:

- Module: DagKernel is an `IPythonKernel` subclass launched by the shipped kernelspec
  (`ipykernel_launcher --IPKernelApp.kernel_class=...`), so no launcher of our own; the three
  additions (analyze_request handler, namespace_delete/namespace_set on execute_request,
  namespace_delta on execute_reply) and how the comm target mirrors them; the `%load_ext`
  path at the bottom of the file.
- `DagKernel` class: why `msg_types` and `control_msg_types` are extended (how
  `Kernel.__init__` builds `shell_handlers` / `control_handlers` from those lists by
  `getattr(self, msg_type)`, and why control is a separate snapshot); the `emit_namespace_delta`
  trait and how `c.DagKernel.emit_namespace_delta` reaches it via traitlets config.
- `__init__` / `_init_dag`: why comm setup is split out (the `%load_ext` path calls it on an
  already-constructed kernel); where `comm_manager` comes from.
- `kernel_info`: that it is a property in ipykernel with no extension hook, so overriding is
  the only way to add JEP 92 `supported_features`; the string spelling convention.
- `analyze_request`: the handler signature ipykernel expects `(stream, ident, parent)` and
  that it is awaited from the dispatch loop; how the reply is sent with `session.send` and
  why `parent` and `ident` matter (routing the reply to the requesting client); why the
  control-channel variant uses the plain `TransformerManager` (control runs on its own
  thread, off the shell's `InteractiveShell`); why a reply is sent even on exception (a
  missing reply hangs the frontend future, which waits for both the reply and the idle
  status).
- `do_execute`: the exact kwargs ipykernel 7 forwards and why extra `execute_request`
  fields must be read from `self.get_parent()`; ordering (snapshot, delete, set, run, diff);
  that the returned dict becomes `execute_reply` content verbatim, which is why
  `namespace_delta` can simply be added; the comm broadcast as the second delivery path.
  Example: the `execute_request` content the frontend sends and the reply it gets back.
- `_comm_analyze`, `_comm_namespace_delete`, `_comm_namespace_set`: the comm request shape
  and that they return only the reply body (DagCommTarget adds `type` and `status`).
- `load_ipython_extension` / `unload_ipython_extension`: the class-swap technique
  (`kernel.__class__ = GeneratedDagKernel`), why a dynamically created subclass is needed
  (DagKernel must come before the running kernel's class in the MRO), why the handler tables
  must be extended by hand (they were built at construction), the limitation that
  `kernel_info` was already answered so the frontend falls back to the comm transport, and
  the attribution to ipyflow. Example: `%load_ext jupyter_dag` in a stock kernel.

Then stop and ask Max to review the file before touching anything else.

## Files 2 to 10 (after the review, in this order, one commit-sized step each)

1. `jupyter_dag/protocol.py`: the wire format; why constants are mirrored by hand in
   `src/dag/protocol.ts` and checked by `tests/test_protocol.py`; each TypedDict is a message
   body, with the message it belongs to.
2. `jupyter_dag/analysis.py`: `transform_cell` (why IPython syntax must be desugared before
   `ast`), the `symtable` walk (module-level symbols, nested scopes, `global` declarations,
   why `del` shows up as assigned and is reported separately, the 3.14 `__annotate__` scope
   filter), why cell magics are opaque, the `dynamic` flag, the builtins filter that only
   `analyze_cells` can apply. Example: `analyze_cell("c", "df = pd.read_csv(path)")`.
3. `jupyter_dag/kernel/namespace.py`: `user_ns` vs `user_ns_hidden` and what IPython hides
   itself; why `del_var(by_name=True)` rather than `pop`; `push(interactive=True)`; the delta
   as a set difference and its blind spot (rebinding is invisible).

   the `{type: ...}` dispatch, why a reply sent inside the handler is correlated by
   `parent_header` on the frontend (no request ids), the `features` message on open, the
   attribution to ipyflow.

   `--IPKernelApp.kernel_class` trick, why the shipped `kernel.json` must equal
   `kernel_json("python")`, how `jupyter_client` rewrites a bare `python` argv[0], the
   frozen-modules flag. Example: `jupyter-dag-kernel install --sys-prefix`.
6. `jupyter_dag/client.py`: how `reqrep(wrapped, fn)` turns a send-function into a
   `reply=True, timeout=` method, why the functions are module-level, the silent empty
   execute as "purge". Example: start the kernel from a temp kernelspec and call
   `analyze` (mirrors `tests/test_kernel.py`).

Python allows reassigning ``__class__`` on an instance when the\n    two classes share a compatible layout, which every ``HasTraits`` subclass without ``__slots__``\n    does. A subclass is created on the fly so that ``DagKernel`` precedes the kernel's existing\n    class in the MRO: ``class GeneratedDagKernel(DagKernel, prev)``. After the swap every method\n    lookup finds the DagKernel overrides first (``do_execute``, ``kernel_info``,\n    ``analyze_request``), and the base class's ``__init__``-time state (session, sockets, comm\n    manager) is untouched because no ``__init__`` runs.\n\n    Two things ``__init__`` would have done must be repeated by hand: :meth:`DagKernel._init_dag`\n    (the comm target), and the handler tables, which ``Kernel.__init__`` filled from the class\n    lists at construction time and which do not consult the class again.
